sections.label: Simultaneous debate voting procedure
sections.summary: The Speaker will put questions on both Motions at the end of the debate and disallow amendments that negative the other Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: As the intent of the Business Motion resolved on 6 February 2023, which is earlier today, is for the House to follow the procedures of previous simultaneous debates, I will put the questions on both Motions at the end of the debate, so that the House can express its views on each Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: In addition, I will also disallow any amendment to either Motion that has the effect of negativing the other Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: By "negativing", the term is to mean the effect of qualifying, transposing, contradicting and nullifying the other Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Any Member who wishes to vote against either Motion can do so directly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: From 2018 to 2022, between 1,000 and 2,900 units of such flats were supplied each year.

sentences.text: In the 10 years from 2012 to 2021, the number of resident marriages each year ranged from 24,000 to 26,000, except in 2020, the year that COVID-19 struck, when it dropped to 21,000.

sections.label: Ramped up BTO supply
sections.summary: The Minister said BTO supply was ramped up to 23,000 flats yearly in 2022 and 2023, with up to 100,000 units from 2021 to 2025 if needed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Minister has said that they have ramped up the BTO supply to launch 23,000 flats each year in 2022 and 2023, and are prepared to launch up to 100,000 units in total over the five-year period, from 2021 to 2025 if needed.

sections.label: HDB units 1981 to 1985

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is especially serious for those in the lowest 20% in terms of income levels, where 96% to 100% of their CPF contributions into the Ordinary Account are used up to pay for the HDB flat.

sections.label: CPF Basic Retirement Sum 2021

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: According to the Minister for Manpower, in 2021, 67% of our CPF members met the Basic Retirement Sum, which pays out about $850 per month.

sections.label: HDB flat land and construction cost
sections.summary: About 60% of a HDB flat's total cost is land cost and the remaining 40% is construction cost.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: About 60% of the total cost of a HDB flat is land cost and the remaining 40% is construction cost.

sections.label: PSP backs singles HDB age 28
sections.summary: PSP supports the Workers' Party proposal to lower the eligibility age for singles to buy HDB flats to 28.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: PSP supports Workers' Party's (WP) proposal to lower the eligibility age for singles to buy HDB flats to 28.

sections.label: PSP housing supply and land cost
sections.summary: PSP calls the 100,000 supply target modest, urges building for projected demand and a deferred land cost model, and asks the Minister questions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The supply target of up to 100,000 over five years from 2021 to 2025 is too modest.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We should be increasing supply more decisively in the immediate term and change to a model of building for projected demand based on factors like marriage and immigration numbers instead of the BTO approach.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As the Chinese saying goes, 羊毛出在羊身上, this means that what appears to be a benefit has actually been paid for in other ways.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We urge the Government to seriously consider the alternative deferred land cost model we are proposing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Given that the first-generation PAP leaders actually sold HDB flats without land cost, in the Minister's opinion, did Mr Lee Kuan Yew and the first-generation PAP leaders raid our reserves?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Lastly, in Annex 7, where he showed the trend of the median household income versus the cost of a 4-room BTO flat, does the Minister agree that using the median household income may not be a good indicator because median household income can change purely based on demographic changes without any change in an individual's wage level?

sections.label: Context on HDB resale market
sections.summary: In contrast to Mr Leong Mun Wai's comment on 11 consecutive quarters of resale prices, the speaker wishes to give context on the HDB resale market.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: In contrast to the Member Mr Leong Mun Wai's comment about the 11th consecutive quarter of the resale price of flats, I wish to put some context on the state of the HDB resale market a few years ago.

sections.label: Robust resale market and imbalance
sections.summary: Five years later, the resale market had been robust for 11 consecutive quarters, with a housing supply and demand imbalance heightened by the pandemic and other factors.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Five years hence – not even a decade, just five years – we have the converse of this issue with a resale market that had been exceedingly robust for 11 consecutive quarters and an imbalance between housing supply and demand heightened by the pandemic and a confluence of other factors.

sections.label: Public flat residents and supply
sections.summary: Over 70% of local residents live in public flats, with flat supply continuing yearly in public and private housing.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Today, we still have more than 70% of local residents living in public flats and the flat supply continues every year both in public and private housing.

sections.label: First-timers resale flat affordability
sections.summary: It asks whether first-timers can afford resale flats in mature estates given lease and subsidy limits on loans.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: The question is – can first-timers afford the price of a resale flat in mature estates when they are unable to take a loan for a longer period because of the remaining flat lease or take a larger loan given the lower subsidy for resale flats?

sections.label: Kampung residents flat resale prices
sections.summary: Residents who bought new flats at about $50,000 now see them resell for $400,000 to $500,000 in mature estates.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Some of my residents, when they relocated from the kampungs, told me that they only purchased their flats at about $50,000 or so and those were actually brand-new flats at that point when they were purchased.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Having lived in the flat for a few decades and looking at the resale market today, these flats would sell – at least, in the mature estate – for a decent price of $400,000 to $500,000.

sections.label: MOP review and resale levy
sections.summary: It asks whether MOP for mature estate BTO flats can be lengthened or a levy placed on profits from sales within 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry also review the Minimum Occupation Period (MOP) for new BTO flats in mature estates to be lengthened and if it cannot and must remain at five years, when the BTO flat is sold within a 10-year timeframe, an additional levy to be placed on those purchasing their next subsidised flat at a percentage of their profit from the sale proceeds?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Speaker, Singapore is one of the few countries in the world where home ownership is extremely high, with more than 90% of citizens owning homes, of which more than 70% actually live in public housing.

sections.label: Balancing affordable housing and land use
sections.summary: It wishes high home ownership to continue for low-income and vulnerable groups, balancing affordable housing against competing land use needs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: I wish this to continues to be so, particularly for our low-income individuals and families and those who are actually vulnerable in society.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: This, in my view, is one of our key challenges as a country and as a people – how best to balance the demand for affordable and accessible housing by Singaporeans against all other competing needs for land use as Singapore continues to modernise.

sections.label: Fears about living in Singapore
sections.summary: Fears about how difficult it is to live in Singapore have been shared many times in the past.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: While the rising prices of groceries or gas may have dominated our more recent conversations, fears of how increasingly difficult it is to live in Singapore have been shared many times in the past.

sections.label: House prices seriously unaffordable
sections.summary: House prices are, according to at least one respected index, seriously unaffordable.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Here, I will only point out that house prices are according to at least one respected index, "seriously unaffordable".

sections.label: HDB and CPF policy cycle
sections.summary: HDB and CPF objectives run counter to each other, and escalating house prices and enhanced grants form a self-reinforcing cycle.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: The two public policy pillars of HDB and CPF have objectives that run counter to each other and tying them together requires an alignment between them, which might not be a problem except that like the proverbial hamster that finds it has to run faster and faster just to keep up with the spinning wheel, we find that escalating house prices, in turn require the Government to keep enhancing the grants it gives out, which in turn allows prices to run away even further, in a never-ending self-reinforcing cycle.

sections.label: Handout to illustrate cycle
sections.summary: The speaker asks permission to circulate a handout illustrating how this plays out.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: A picture tells a thousand words, so with your permission, Mr Speaker, I would like to circulate a handout to illustrate how this plays out.

sections.label: Inflation and house price spike
sections.summary: As inflation rises the curve rises more but plunges more after the peak, so recent inflation is at least partially responsible for the house price spike.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: First of all, observe how as inflation rises, the curve rises more but the plunge is also more significant once we pass the peak.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: So, inflation, such as the bout that we have experienced lately, is at least partially responsible for the spike we see in house prices.

sections.label: Bubble doubling prices, rental jump
sections.summary: At the peak house prices would be more than double those without the bubble, so the 30% jump in private rental rates last year should worry all.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: At the peak, house prices would be more than double what they would be in the absence of this bubble.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: That is why, even though the overwhelming majority of Singaporeans do not rent, the eye-watering 30% jump in private rental rates last year should worry all of us.

sections.label: Land prices and BTO prices
sections.summary: If land prices are indirectly derived from the HDB resale market using transaction prices as comparables, any bubble there becomes embedded in BTO prices.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: If land prices are indirectly derived from the HDB resale market with transaction prices used as comparables, then any bubble in that market would become embedded into our BTO prices.

sections.label: Breaking land valuation market link
sections.summary: Breaking the link between land valuation and market comparables deflates the bubble component in land pricing.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: The key is to break the tight link between land valuation that takes reference to market comparables and thereby deflate the bubble component that could build up in land pricing.

sections.label: Land charge for roads, transitways
sections.summary: The land charge for roads and transitways is $1 a metre given their inherent public nature.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Recognising the inherent public nature of roads and transitways, the land charge for this group is a mere $1 a metre.

sections.label: New homebuyers pay land cost
sections.summary: New homebuyers pay more for BTO and resale flats, with a significant part going to land cost channelled into reserves.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: The Government is asking new homebuyers today to pay more for their BTO and resale flats, a significant part of which goes towards land cost, which in turn, is channelled into the reserves.

sections.label: Buying excess leases, buyback scheme
sections.summary: The Government may buy up excess leases up to 30 years, while the Workers' Party proposed a universal sale and lease buyback scheme.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: In this case, the Government may need to step in to buy up excess leases, perhaps up to 30 years, to provide a cushion.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: The Workers' Party, on its part, has proposed a universal sale and lease buyback scheme, which differs in that we do not require a return of lease buyback balance into CPF.

sections.label: Expanded public housing scheme details
sections.summary: Louis Chua shared a public housing scheme expanding rentals to larger units, relaxing eligibility, with a time limit to minimise abuse.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: My Sengkang colleague, Mr Louis Chua, has previously shared details on a more comprehensive public housing scheme which would expand rentals to include larger format units and relax the eligibility criteria.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Add to this a time limit which will further minimise potential abuse, this scheme will ensure a roof over the heads of those families who wish to eventually own but allow them to wait out until the market reset is complete.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: While we do need to alleviate backlogs, in the near future, this strategy will prevent overbuilding —

sections.label: Sim Ann on expanded public rentals
sections.summary: Sim Ann pushed back against expanded public rentals, suggesting it could weaken communities, and distinguished renting from leasing.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: In a response to Mr Louis Chua's speech, Senior Minister of State Sim Ann pushed back against the notion of expanded public rentals, suggesting that it could weaken our communities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Rental is essentially choosing to rent month-to-month or year-to-year whereas leasing is to pay upfront.

sections.label: Housing options and retirement adequacy
sections.summary: A wider range of housing options is needed for Singaporeans at different life and career stages to sever the link between affordable housing and retirement adequacy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: The bottom line is that we need to afford a wider range of housing options for Singaporeans who may be at different stages of their lives and careers to allow them to sever what is clearly becoming an ever more untenable link between affordable housing and retirement adequacy.

sections.label: State land is not free
sections.summary: Land is not free just because it is state land.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Land is not free just because it is state land.

sections.label: Omitting land value from housing cost
sections.summary: Omitting or deferring land value when computing public housing cost writes off investments in the economy, society, environment, planning, infrastructure and maintenance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To omit or defer the value of land when computing the cost of our public housing means we are writing off generations of investment into our economy, society and environment, writing off the direct investments in planning, infrastructure and maintenance, writing off the value on behalf of past, present and future generations of Singaporeans.

sections.label: Land value in public housing costs
sections.summary: Factoring land value into public housing costs closes the loop of value creation and value capture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Factoring in land value into the costs of public housing closes the loop of value creation and value capture.

sections.label: Singaporeans in public housing
sections.summary: In Singapore, roughly 80% of Singaporeans live in public housing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In Singapore, roughly 80% of Singaporeans live in public housing.

sections.label: Subsidies for mature estate housing
sections.summary: Bringing down prices in mature estates or providing more grants leads to more subsidies from taxpayers' money or the reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The call to either bring down the prices inmature estates or provide more grants to make them more accessible will ultimately lead to the same things – more subsidies in the form of taxpayers' money or tapping into the reserves.

sections.label: SERS project government losses
sections.summary: The Government cannot run huge losses for each SERS project.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government cannot run huge losses for each SERS project.

sections.label: Government impartiality and SERS methodology
sections.summary: The Government maintains impartiality across SERS projects, and the methodology should not be modified at will.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It also maintains impartiality as the Government moves from one SERS project to another.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We should not allow the methodology to be modified at will because it is equivalent to having the Government dictate values arbitrarily.

sections.label: Countries charmed by appealing rhetoric
sections.summary: Many examples exist worldwide of countries charmed by appealing rhetoric that understates trade-offs and real costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In recent past, we can see many examples around the world of how countries would get charmed by appealing rhetoric that understates the trade-offs and real costs.

sections.label: Trade-offs, reserves and HDB flats
sections.summary: People may not believe the trade-offs are real, and HDB is prepared to launch up to 100,000 flats from 2021 to 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Sometimes, I think people do not believe the trade-offs we are grappling with are real.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It seems they believe we can just tap into our reserves to pay the trade-offs away.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In business, every promise for a reward is usually accompanied by a corresponding risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When we look at business deals, the ones that are too good to be true usually are.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: HDB is prepared to launch up to 100,000 flats in total from 2021 to 2025, if needed.

sections.label: HDB resale price increases
sections.summary: In 2022 HDB resale prices rose 10.4%, and over three years they rose 31%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For the full year 2022, HDB resale prices saw another year of double-digit price increases at 10.4% compared to a year ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In the last three years, HDB resale prices rose by a whopping 31%.

sections.label: BTO supply fall 2024 2025
sections.summary: Launching all 100,000 flats from 2021 to 2025 implies BTO supply falls 20% to about 18,400 flats in 2024 and 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even if HDB decides to launch the whole 100,000 flats in total from 2021 to 2025, this implies that BTO supply falls 20% to about 18,400 flats in 2024 and 2025.

sections.label: Private housing and EC supply
sections.summary: Government increased confirmed-list private housing and EC supply 75% from about 3,600 units in 2021 to around 6,300 in 2022, and 17% half-on-half in first half 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Again, I note that in percentage terms, the Government has increased the supply of private housing, including Executive Condominiums (ECs) on the confirmed list of the Government Land Sales (GLS) programme by 75%, from about 3,600 units in 2021 to around 6,300 units in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In the first half of the 2023 GLS programme, the number of units has also increased by about 17% half-on-half to about 4,100 units.

sections.label: BTO flats versus citizen marriages
sections.summary: Over the last 10 years up to 2021, citizen marriages totalled about 230,000 while HDB BTO flats launched were only about 192,000 units.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To put into context once again, the number of BTO flats launched, the number of citizen marriages was cumulatively about 230,000 over the last 10 years up to 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, the number of HDB BTO flats launched was only about 192,000 units or so in the same period.

sections.label: Housing supply increase and BTO launches
sections.summary: Housing supply is set to rise about 35% over 2022 and 2023 with about 23,000 BTO flats yearly, and HDB may launch up to 100,000 flats from 2021 to 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Since this is the Government's position, it is only natural for us to believe that the Government can effectively implement this strategy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I acknowledge that compared to 2021, housing supply is set to increase by about 35% over 2022 and 2023, with about 23,000 BTO flats to be launched per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Moreover, HDB stated that it is prepared to launch up to 100,000 flats in total from 2021 to 2025, if needed, subject to prevailing demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even if the HDB decides to launch the whole 100,000 flats in total from 2021 to 2025, this implies that BTO supply falls 20% to about 18,400 flats in 2024 and 2025.

sections.label: High BTO application rates
sections.summary: Despite supply ramp-up in the past two years, overall application rates stayed high at 5.1 times in 2022, indicating demand-supply imbalance remains a critical concern.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: What is of greater concern is that despite the supposed ramp-up in supply in the past two years, overall application rates have remained stubbornly high at 5.1 times in 2022, suggesting that the level of demand-supply imbalance remains a critical concern.

sections.label: Home ownership and HDB residence
sections.summary: About 80% of citizens own their own homes today, and 80% of Singapore's resident population live in HDB public housing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: About 80% of citizens own their own homes today, one of the highest home ownerships in the world, and 80% of Singapore's resident population live in HDB public housing.

sections.label: Delayed marriage and PLH programme
sections.summary: Some in serious relationships delay marriage and children until they get permanent housing, and the Government implemented the PLH programme with longer MOP, tighter rental restrictions and subsidy recovery.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Yet, others who are more serious in their relationships decide that they would delay marriage and having children until they procure their permanent housing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I commend the Government for having the political will and courage to implement the latest Prime Location Public Housing (PLH) programme, with features, such as the longer MOP, tighter rental restrictions and recovering of additional subsidies.

sections.label: Additional buyer stamp duty on properties
sections.summary: The Government introduced additional buyer stamp duty to tax purchases of second and subsequent residential properties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Two, continue with the additional buyer stamp duty (ABSD) introduced by the Government to tax the purchase of second and subsequent residential properties.

sections.label: Building appealing satellite towns
sections.summary: Build more appealing satellite towns away from popular estates with better residential concepts, education facilities, business hubs and transport amenities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: One, build even more appealing satellite towns away from the popular estates through better residential concepts, better education facilities, business hubs and transport amenities.

sections.label: Incentives for non-mature estates
sections.summary: Provide more substantive financial and non-financial incentives, especially for first-time BTO applicants, to move to non-mature estates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Two, provide more substantive financial and non-financial incentives especially for first-time BTO applicants to move to non-mature estates.

sections.label: HDB historical cost clawback
sections.summary: HDB will record a flat's historical cost, clawed back when the buyer sells, making a $350,000 Tengah flat go for $140,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: HDB will then record the historical cost of this flat which will then be clawed back when a buyer decides to sell.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This way, according to Mr Leong, a Tengah flat, which is quoted at $350,000 would go for $140,000.

sections.label: Bishan BTO versus private property
sections.summary: A Bishan BTO costs about $500 to $600 per square foot, while Skyview private property across the road costs $1,700 per square foot.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: A Bishan BTO today costs about $500 to $600 per square foot, while a private property just across the road at Skyview costs $1,700 per square foot – more than double the BTO price.

sections.label: Affordable Homes Scheme taxpayer cost
sections.summary: The passage asks how much the Affordable Homes Scheme would cost taxpayers, especially Singaporeans who do not enjoy it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: How much would the Affordable Homes Scheme cost in total to taxpayers, especially to Singaporeans who do not get to enjoy it?

sections.label: Arm's length accounting principle
sections.summary: An accountant states that accounting requires arm's length transactions, where goods and services are provided, sold or transferred at prevailing market prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: As an accountant, I can tell you there is a fundamental basic principle in accounting, which is that everything must be done at arm's length.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: It is called an arm's length transaction, that is, goods and services must be provided, sold or transferred at arm's length prevailing market prices.

sections.label: Land sale and reserves
sections.summary: Selling land to the private sector puts proceeds into reserves for investment and NIRC, so giving it to HDB below market price depletes reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: If he sells it to the private sector, we all know there is a Government Land Sale, the proceeds would then go into reserves and then it is invested and that is where we get our Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC).

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: So, if you just give it to HDB at $1 or less than the market price, you are in effect depleting the reserves.

sections.label: Land price and BTO prices
sections.summary: Land must be priced at the prevailing market price assessed by the Chief Valuer, and lower BTO and resale prices could result.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: So, because of that, there must be a price to the land cost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: And the price must therefore be the prevailing market price as assessed by the Chief Valuer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Because some of the arguments put up by Mr Leong, I think, whilst I am no property expert and neither is he, I think it is going to lead to a decrease in BTO prices, it is going to lead to a decrease in resale prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I think if my memory serves me right – in 2003 and 2004, after the 1997 Financial Crisis, there were unsold HDB flats; tens of thousands of them.

sections.label: Caution on housing wishes
sections.summary: The speaker says it will take a long time and warns to be careful what you wish for, as 89% of Singaporeans are home owners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: It is going to take you a long time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: So, again, be careful what you wish for, especially in Singapore where 89% of our population are home owners.

sections.label: Bidadari new dwelling units
sections.summary: By end-2025 there will be 9,000 new dwelling units in Bidadari, with flats sold at about six to seven times family household income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: By the end of 2025, there will be 9,000 new dwelling units in Bidadari.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: Based on my estimation, I think the flats are sold at not mean household income, but the family household income, about maybe six times, maximum seven.

sections.label: Long waiting time for flats
sections.summary: Residents report long waiting times, mainly due to COVID-19, and Minister Desmond Lee says ways are being sought to solve this soon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: The problem is the long waiting time, as residents at Meet-the-People Sessions have told me and emailed me.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: But the key reason for the long waiting time is because of COVID-19 and as Minister Desmond Lee has said, we are looking for ways to solve this as soon as possible.

sections.label: Singapore home ownership rate
sections.summary: Singapore has a very high rate of home ownership of 90%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Today, as hon Members before me have said, Singapore has a very high rate of home ownership of 90%.

sections.label: 2020 report on Singapore housing
sections.summary: A 2020 report said over 80% of Singapore residents own and live in HDB public housing, addressing 1960s housing problems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In its 2020 report on Singapore, the authors made the following points: (a) more than 80% of Singapore residents own and live in public housing provided by HDB; and (b) this addressed the housing unaffordability and accessibility problem that we encountered in the 1960s.

sections.label: OECD lowest quintile housing spending
sections.summary: An average household in the lowest quintile of an OECD country spends 37% of income on housing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: An average household in the lowest quintile of an OECD country spends 37% of the household income on housing.

sections.label: Government subsidies and grants for homes
sections.summary: The Minister explained Government subsidies and grants let most Singaporeans buy homes about five times their annual incomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The hon Minister had recently explained that the Government provides subsidies and grants to allow the vast majority of Singaporeans to purchase homes which are about five times their annual incomes and he also mentions that this compares very favourably to cities like London, Los Angeles, Sydney and of course, Hong Kong too.

sections.label: HDB building 100,000 units
sections.summary: HDB is building 100,000 units between 2021 and 2025, which is the forecast demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: HDB, as we heard from the hon Minister, is dealing with the problem decisively by building 100,000 units between 2021 and 2025, and that, I understand, is the forecast of the demand.

sections.label: Median waiting time for flats
sections.summary: Singapore's median waiting time is between four and 4.5 years, expected to fall below three years by 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In Singapore, the median waiting time is between four and 4.5 years and is expected to come down to below three years by 2024.

sections.label: Lowest rental range monthly rates
sections.summary: For those earning $800 or less who have not owned subsidised housing, the rate is between $26 and $33 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: At the lowest range, for those who earn $800 or less and have not owned subsidised housing before, it is between $26 and $33 per month.

sections.label: Rental households becoming homeowners
sections.summary: In the past decade, 7,800 rental households have progressed to home ownership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In the past decade alone, 7,800 rental households have progressed to home ownership.

sections.label: Median unit price and total
sections.summary: The median is about $411,000 per unit, and multiplying the units gives a figure of at least $40 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: As a median, it is about $411,000 per unit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: If you were to just multiply the units, I get a figure of at least $40 billion.

sections.label: Housing figure versus annual budget
sections.summary: The annual budget spend is about $100 billion, while this comes in at $40-plus billion at market rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Just to give you some comparison, our spend for our annual budget is about $100 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This is coming in at $40-plus billion just at market rate.

sections.label: Human capital index and housing
sections.summary: Singapore ranks best in the World Bank Human Capital Index, with a child born today 88% as productive when she grows up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In the most recent World Bank Human Capital Index, Singapore ranks as the best country in the world in human capital development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: A child born today in Singapore will be 88% as productive when she grows up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I have no doubt that this percentage is contributed in part because of our successful housing policy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This is an encouraging statistic but more can be done to develop our children in stable and conducive housing environments that will allow them to be the best they can be.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: From time to time, I come across cases involving single mothers, with their children in tow, asking for urgent housing assistance because they have consented to the division of matrimonial properties in divorce proceedings, which in my respectful view, does not adequately take care of the needs of their children —

sections.label: Murali Pillai's $40 billion figure
sections.summary: Mr Murali Pillai shared a figure of $40 billion, which he said he got from the HDB annual report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Mr Murali Pillai shared a figure of $40 billion, which he said he got from the HDB annual report.

sections.label: Cumulative Government grants to HDB
sections.summary: Cumulative Government grants to HDB since its establishment in 1960 amounted to $42 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The cumulative Government grants to HDB since its establishment in 1960 amounted to $42 billion.

sections.label: Supply of BTO units
sections.summary: The speaker says 20,000 units a year averaged over 2021 to 2025 appears inadequate given marriages and new citizens.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As to how many should be built, I think that will require a lot more information than I have available on what is the current backlog.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But I do want to make the point that considering that the number of resident marriages every year is 24,000 to 26,000 and new citizen numbers are about 20,000 a year, the supply of 20,000 units a year averaged over 2021 to 2025 does appear inadequate.

sections.label: Building volume and resale prices
sections.summary: The speaker asks how resale flat prices can keep up if large building volumes continue given ageing population and lower fertility.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: Can I confirm whether that is the Government's approach?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: I think I was quite specific in that I said given the fact that we have an ageing population and also a lower total fertility rate, if we were to continue building the supply in the same volume which Ms Hazel Poa referred to 40 years ago – I cannot remember the exact number, but it was like building 189,000 flats – if we continue in those large volumes, my question was how would we actually be able to ensure that the resale flat prices can continue to keep up if you indefinitely build this kind of volume?

sections.label: Shorter wait time BTO units
sections.summary: In 2021 and 2022 HDB launched 4- and 5-room BTO units with shorter wait times, with the shortest being two-and-a-half years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Indeed, in the November 2021 exercise alone, there were more than 2,000 4- and 5-room BTO units, or almost 20% of all 4- and 5-room units launched across 2021, with shorter wait times of around three-and-a-half years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Then, last year, in 2022, HDB launched almost 5,000 4- and 5-room BTO units, more than double the number in 2021, with shorter wait times of 3.8 years or less.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: These units made up almost 30% of all 4- and 5-room BTO units launched in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And the shortest wait time amongst these was two-and-a-half years, with 1,300 units available.

sections.label: First-timer application rates in 2022
sections.summary: In 2022, more than 9,000 4- and 5-room BTO units had first-timer application rates of three times or lower across nine projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: In 2022, more than 9,000, or almost 60% of all 4- and 5-room BTO units launched had first-timer application rates of three times or lower across nine different projects.

sections.label: Ang Mo Kio Central Weave prices
sections.summary: In the August 2022 BTO exercise, Ang Mo Kio Central Weave 4-room units started at $535,000 and 5-room units at $720,000 before grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: In the August 2022 BTO exercise, there was much public interest in Ang Mo Kio Central Weave, where 4-room units started at $535,000 and 5-room units at $720,000, before grants.

sections.label: 4-room BTO price cap
sections.summary: The speaker suggests keeping 4-room BTO prices at five times median income, just under $500,000 before grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: In my mind, this means keeping the price of a 4-room BTO to five times of median income, or just under $500,000, before grants.

sections.label: 5-room BTO price cap
sections.summary: The speaker suggests capping 5-room BTO prices at $650,000 before grants, based on a price-to-income ratio of five.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Again, at a home price to income ratio of five, this works out to $650,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And so, my suggestion is to cap the price of a 5-room BTO to $650,000, before grants.

sections.label: Higher subsidies with longer MOP
sections.summary: The speaker suggests higher subsidies for more projects, lower BTO launch prices, a 10-year MOP and 6% subsidy recovery at resale.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Apply higher subsidies to more projects like Ang Mo Kio Central Weave, push down the BTO launch prices to be within reach of most Singaporeans, but attach the longer Minimum Occupation Period (MOP) of 10 years, and the subsidy recovery of 6% at point of resale.

sections.label: Subsidy tiers with MOP recovery
sections.summary: The speaker describes subsidy tiers between basic and PLH levels, with MOPs of six, seven years and recoveries of 2%, 3%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Basically, the "basic" level of subsidies, five-year MOP, zero subsidy recovery on one end; and PLH-level subsidies, 10-year MOP, 6% subsidy recovery on the other end.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: But in between, we could have a subsidy tier, with six-year MOP and 2% recovery, another higher subsidy tier, seven-year MOP, 3% recovery and so on.

sections.label: Calculated figure of $380,000
sections.summary: The speaker states that if their calculations are right, it comes to about $380,000 at current income levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: If my calculations are right, it comes up to about $380,000 at current income levels.

sections.label: First-timer application success rates
sections.summary: The speaker states 60% or 9,000 of 4-room and 5-room flats launched in 2022 did not exceed an application rate of three.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Looking at the figures for first-timers in 2022, 60% or 9,000 units of the 4-room and 5-room flats launched last year did not exceed the application rate of three, which means that first-timers stand a good chance of success in applying for a 4-room or 5-room flat.

sections.label: Pandemic delay in waiting time
sections.summary: Waiting time is quite long, with a current median of 4.3 years, due to the delay caused by the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: In this respect, due to the delay caused by the pandemic, waiting time is indeed quite long with the current median of 4.3 years.

sections.label: BTO development cost and HDB deficit
sections.summary: Land and construction costs make up total development cost of BTO projects, and MOF grants cover HDB's deficit, a cumulative $40 billion since 1960.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And so, I stand in full support of the Motion, standing in the name of the Minister for National Development and affirm the long-standing and continued commitment of the Government to our public housing objectives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: I have checked and I just want to clarify that the land cost together with construction costs, make up total development cost of BTO projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: HDB's proceeds from BTO sales cannot fully recover this development cost, MOF grants are being given to HDB to make up for this deficit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: The $40 billion which I referred to is a cumulative deficit since HDB's formation in 1960 and that would comprise some payments for land, but not entirely.

sections.label: Breakdown of $350,000 flat
sections.summary: For a $350,000 flat, $140,000 was the price at purchase and $210,000 may be payment for land at sale.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The breakdown he used was for a $350,000 flat, $140,000 would be the price for the flat at the time of purchase and $210,000 may be the payment made for the land at the time of sale.

sections.label: Leong proposal land cost payment
sections.summary: Under Mr Leong's proposal, everyone who sells their flat must pay land cost, a lump sum, so most pay more than under the current scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Under Mr Leong's proposal, the upshot is that for everyone who chooses to sell their flats, they will now be required to pay land cost, something they were not previously required to, which will be a huge lump sum payment at the time of sale.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I think it is common ground, then, that most people will end up paying more for their flat at the time they sell than they currently do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, for everyone who sells their flats, which is the majority of Singaporeans, they will pay more under Mr Leong's proposal than under the current scheme.

sections.label: Families needing cash to sell
sections.summary: Families without several hundred thousand dollars in cash readily available will not be able to sell their flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: If families do not have several hundred thousand dollars in cash readily available, they will not be able to sell their flats.

sections.label: PSP proposal resale market effect
sections.summary: The effect of PSP's proposal on the resale market is uncertain, and the real reason for the resale price spike is limited supply relative to demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The truth is that the effect of PSP's proposal on the resale market is uncertain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I believe, the real reason for the spike in resale prices now is the limited supply relative to demand.

sections.label: PSP proposal market distorting effects
sections.summary: The speaker says the PSP proposal would distort the market, add to BTO queues and impose a massive selling fee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Ultimately, I believe this proposal proposed by the PSP and supported by Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, would have even more distorting effects on the market, adding to the long queues at BTO launches and saddling all of them with a massive fee when they want to sell, which means they actually pay more than current flat owners.

sections.label: Home ownership versus renting
sections.summary: The speaker says property ownership lets Singaporeans benefit from economic growth and that a nation of renters is not a good substitute.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Currently, the fact that Singaporeans are able to get onto the property ownership ladder allows all of them to enjoy and benefit from Singapore's economic growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I believe home ownership is a worthwhile aspiration for our Government to support and making us a nation of home renters is not a good substitute.

sections.label: HDB flat prices and subsidies
sections.summary: The speaker says flat prices did not fall in a straight line by lease and most BTO owners still gain on sale due to subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: They did not fall in a straight line based on their lease.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Also, because HDB flats are sold at a subsidised price, most homeowners will continue to enjoy an upside if they sell their BTO flats in their lifetime.

sections.label: Removing MOP for resale flats
sections.summary: The speaker suggests removing the Minimum Occupation Period for resale flats, keeping Seller's Stamp Duties, to ease BTO queues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This brings me to a suggestion I had previously made.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I think we should take off at least one of the property cooling measures for the resale market that I believe may be driving prices up instead, namely, the Minimum Occupation Period (MOP) for resale flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I do not think it is necessary for those who bought resale flats at fair market value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I believe the unintended consequence of this measure is that the supply of resale flats is restricted, because every transaction results in a resale flat being taken off the market for five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I think it is still fair to retain the Seller's Stamp Duties to prevent pure speculation, but without the MOP, which prevents the sale altogether.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I believe that if resale prices moderate such that buying a flat in the resale market is comparable to the price of a BTO flat once resale subsidies are priced in, the long queue for BTO flats would ameliorate.

sections.label: Poll on property affordability
sections.summary: The speaker cites a poll of 790 respondents finding nearly 60% find property unaffordable, with BTO launches oversubscribed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In fact, nearly six in 10 or 60% of people want to rent or buy, so they find property becoming more unaffordable, according to a poll of 790 respondents conducted in July last year by a private company that provides online services for home rentals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is because the most affordable type of HDB flat – the BTO flat – is seeing excess demand, many launches substantially oversubscribed.

sections.label: HDB flats as homes
sections.summary: The speaker says mindsets should be reframed to treat HDB flats primarily as affordable homes rather than rising assets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Facing these two realities, I think the time has come for us to reboot, refresh and reframe mindsets and start thinking of our HDB flats as primarily a home to live in, an affordable home and much less of an asset whose value will rise and rise in the same way that the value of, for example, developed country equities.

sections.label: HDB flats as homes
sections.summary: The speaker argues HDB flats should be viewed first as affordable homes, not appreciating retirement assets, since finite leases must eventually expire.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Rising property prices can also suck away household capital from other uses like financing a spell away from the workforce to retrain or pursue a further degree, for example – something that is very relevant in this age of disruption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, rather than focus on rising HDB flat prices to uplift the generations, I believe we should rewire our thinking to once again view HDB flats as, first and foremost, an affordable home to live in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: More specifically, does the Government designate HDB flats as a retirement asset which necessitates their appreciation of the time even though the inherent nature of the finite lease requires that they must eventually depreciate and expire zero?

sections.label: HPI averages 2022
sections.summary: HPI in 2022 ranged from 5.7 to 4.2, averaging four for BTO flats and 5.1 for resale flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: HPI in 2022 ranged from 5.7 to 4.2.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The average for BTO flats was four and the average for resale flats was 5.1.

sections.label: HPI for non-mature BTOs
sections.summary: Annex 2 puts the HPI for BTO flats in non-mature estates at around 4.5 for 3-room and 5.5 for 5-room flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Annex 2, which Minister Desmond Lee circulated, puts the HPI for BTO flats in non-mature estates now at around 4.5 for 3-room flats and 5.5 for 5-room flats.

sections.label: Resale prices and TFR
sections.summary: A 2021 paper by NUS PhD student Kidjie Saguin found a statistically significant link between higher resale prices and lower TFR in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A PhD student at NUS Kidjie Saguin in a paper she authored for the Asian Development Bank Institute in March 2021 found a statistically significant link between higher resale prices and lower TFR in Singapore.

sections.label: BTO flats with 70-year leases
sections.summary: The speaker suggests the Government consider building BTO flats sold at 70-year leases with an option to top up 29 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First of all, Sir, I would like to suggest that the Government consider building some BTO flats sold at 70-year leases with the option to top up to another 29 years.

sections.label: Tiered BTOs and shorter leases
sections.summary: This would give HDB a five-year planning window for the site, and tiered BTOs would be sold significantly cheaper due to shorter leases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This would allow a five-year planning window for HDB to decide how best to deal with the site.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Certainly, tiered BTOs like this would be sold at a significantly cheaper price due to the shorter lease duration.

sections.label: Shorter Wait Time BTO proportion
sections.summary: Minister Desmond Lee said the proportion of Shorter Wait Time BTOs will rise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Minister Desmond Lee also yesterday said that the proportion of Shorter Wait Time BTOs will rise.

sections.label: House price index comparison question
sections.summary: A speaker asks whether the HPI comparison to London, Los Angeles and Sydney covers all home transactions and apartments of similar size to HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Before I end my speech, I have some clarifications for Minister Desmond Lee and his Annex 9, which compares the house price index (HPI) in Singapore to several cities with very high house prices such as London, Los Angeles and Sydney.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My question is: are the HPIs in these cities based on all home transactions, including landed homes in those cities?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Would the Minister have the HPI in those cities for apartments with the same average square footage as HDB flats in Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I think that would be a more useful apples-to-apples comparison and I hope the Minister or the Government can share this information, if possible, during the course of today's debate.

sections.label: 25% debt service ratio cap
sections.summary: The 25% debt service ratio formula in the 2020 manifesto is a maximum cap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: The 25% debt service ratio formula expressed in our manifesto in 2020 is a maximum cap.

sections.label: 2020 manifesto elements and HPI target
sections.summary: The 2020 manifesto formulation includes a 20-year tenure, 10% downpayment and subsidies for 2- and 3-room flats, with an HPI target of three for BTOs in non-mature estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: But he is referring to the 2020 manifesto's formulation that we gave and I would remind him that it includes various elements which he did not allude to – a 20-year tenure, a 10% downpayment and additional subsidies for 2- and 3-room flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: We have said that we believe that three or close to three is the right HPI target for BTO in a non-mature estate.

sections.label: Affordability criteria and BTO subsidies
sections.summary: The affordability criteria is an HPI of three for a BTO in a non-mature estate, and rising land valuation requires bigger subsidies, from $1.5 billion to close to $4 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: To Mr Xie, I would reply that I have stated what that criteria of affordability is several times in my speech and several times in my exchange with you.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: It is a HPI of three for a BTO in a non-mature estate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: You did not answer my other question, which is if we have an ever appreciating cycle of property prices that lead to higher BTO prices because the land valuation goes up and we still want to keep BTOs affordable, that needs bigger and bigger subsidies from the Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: I think $1.5 billion, it has gone up to close to $4 billion and it is going to go up even more.

sections.label: Bequest motive and renting flats
sections.summary: Qualitative research suggests the bequest motive is important, and not everyone wants or is able to rent out their flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: My understanding of that is that there is some qualitative research that suggest that the bequest motive, parents wanting to leave the flat to their children, is a very, very important reason.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: I am not aware of any statistical survey that has been done – to be fair to Mr Pillai's question – but I believe that there is some qualitative evidence on the table.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Certainly, from my conversations with constituents, with Singaporeans who are in that older category who would qualify for the LBS, I have found from those conversations that many of them are very worried about an environment of ever-increasing property prices that their children will have to face in later years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: And therefore, they want to keep that flat, pass on to their children, in view of their lack of confidence that houses will continue to be affordable for their children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: The second question that Mr Pillai asked was — there was only one question?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: So, I think in my speech, and to address Mr Pillai more holistically, other than wanting to leave your flat to your children, there is also the fact that not everyone wants to rent out their flat or is able to rent out their flat.

sections.label: Parliament role and PSP Motion
sections.summary: Speaker says Parliament should flag policy areas needing change but cannot support the PSP Motion because its wording suggests Government public housing policies do not deliver these objectives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And it is precisely the role of Parliament and Parliamentarians to point out areas of public policy that should be revisited and changed if they are not working or not working optimally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, I find that I am not able to support the PSP’s Motion because the manner it is worded suggests that the Government public housing policies at this point do not deliver on these objectives or do not even have these as objectives.

sections.label: Rejecting Leong's land cost proposal
sections.summary: Speaker says Government rebuttals speak for themselves and disagrees with Mr Leong's proposal to exempt buyers from paying purported land cost until they sell their flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These rebuttals have been made by the Government and speak for themselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I further do not agree with the hon Members Mr Leong’s proposal in his speech, in particular, that buyers be exempted from paying the purported land cost of their flats until they sell their flat.

sections.label: Prime Location Public Housing scheme
sections.summary: Speaker cites the Prime Location Public Housing scheme, which gives higher subsidies for flats in prime locations like the Greater Southern Waterfront so they are more accessible to a wider range of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If we look at one such policy – the Prime Location Public Housing scheme, which gives higher subsidies for flats in prime locations like the Greater Southern Waterfront, so that they become more accessible to a wider range of Singaporeans.

sections.label: Safeguards against lottery effect
sections.summary: Speaker says he initially thought buyers could strike a lottery, but the Government added safeguards including a higher Minimum Occupation Period and a subsidy recovery mechanism even after a 10-year period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My first impression reading about the scheme when it was first mooted was that some buyers would strike a lottery if they win the ballot for these flats, as, after having taken advantage of the higher subsidies, they would be able to get a windfall when they sell the flat after the Minimum Occupation Period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, when the scheme was eventually rolled out, the Government layered a safeguard against precisely this “lottery effect”, including a higher Minimum Occupation Period and a subsidy recovery mechanism even when the flat is sold after a 10-year period.

sections.label: Impact of choice location flats
sections.summary: Speaker says these larger flats in choice locations are only 1% to 2% of sales, so their impact on other new or resale flats is minimal and they are not indicative of flats generally becoming unaffordable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They are larger and they are in choice locations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They also make up a very small proportion of the total number of sales – I understand just between 1% and 2%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Their impact on the price of new flats or resale flats that do not have these characteristics, is minimal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As such, while these make the headlines, they are not indicative of flats, in general, becoming unaffordable.

sections.label: Minister on reserves raid
sections.summary: Speaker says the Minister addressed these proposals in Parliament last month and explained the proposal would amount to a raid on the reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The hon Minister had addressed these proposals in Parliament last month and explained how this proposal would amount to a raid on the reserves.

sections.label: Leong conflates Government accounts
sections.summary: Mr Leong continued to conflate the Government's accounts with the past reserves in his speech yesterday.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In fact, in his speech yesterday, Mr Leong continued to conflate the Government's accounts with the past reserves.

sections.label: Populist propositions gain public traction
sections.summary: The speaker expects an incorrect but simplistic populist proposition to gain more public agreement than a correct but complex explanation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When faced with a correct but more technical and complex explanation as the Minister had made, which may take some time and thought to understand, as compared to an incorrect but simplistic and far more delicious proposition, I expect that the delicious proposition, the nod to a populist position, will have more traction and agreement amongst the public.

sections.label: Housing policies as social economic policies
sections.summary: The speaker says housing policies are social and economic policies and cannot support the PSP Motion's proposals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As I had mentioned, our housing policies are also a set of social and economic policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is often meaningless to look at just one factor, criticise it and make suggestions on how to change it, without looking at the whole.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The PSP Motion and its related proposals does precisely this and I therefore find myself unable to support it.

sections.label: PAP votes-for-upgrading in 2006
sections.summary: PAP candidates promised $180 million of upgrading projects for Hougang and Potong Pasir in the 2006 election.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The PAP's votes-for-upgrading election strategy continued into the 2006 election when PAP candidates promised $180 million of upgrading projects for Hougang and Potong Pasir if voters tossed out the Opposition there and voted for the PAP.

sections.label: HDB resale flat price increase
sections.summary: HDB resale flat prices increased 382% in value from 1990 to 2010.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: HDB resale flat prices increased 382% in value from 1990 to 2010.

sections.label: Ageing flats and declining value
sections.summary: Perpetual property price increases are unsustainable, and about 70,000 flats over 40 years old will decline in value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Yet, perpetual property price increases are neither sustainable nor in the public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There are currently about 70,000 flats that are more than 40 years old, with remaining leases of 59 years or less.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These flats will decline in value after the 50- to 60-year mark, as illustrated by Assoc Prof Jamus Lim yesterday.

sections.label: Resale HDB price-to-income ratio
sections.summary: The median house price to income ratio after grants for first-timer families buying resale HDB flats in the last five years was between 4.6 and 5.0.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The median house price to income ratio or HPI after grants for first-timer families who bought a resale HDB flat in the last five years was between 4.6 and 5.0.

sections.label: Older owners of larger flats
sections.summary: As at 2021, 71,000 flats of 3-room or larger were owned by married persons over 65 whose children had moved out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As at 2021, there were 71,000 flats that are 3-room or larger which were owned by married persons over the age of 65 whose children had moved out.

sections.label: BTO 2-room Flexi application rates
sections.summary: As at September 2022, application rates for BTO 2-room Flexi flats for elderly households ranged from 2.0 to 4.6 times in non-mature estates and 9.9 times in mature estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The application rates of BTO 2-room Flexi flats allocated to elderly households as at September 2022, ranged from 2.0 to 4.6 times in non-mature estates, and 9.9 times in mature estates.

sections.label: HDB owners with private property
sections.summary: As at October 2022, about 3% of HDB flat owners owned at least one private property.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As at October 2022, about 3% of HDB flat owners owned at least one private property.

sections.label: ABSD rebate for selling HDB flat
sections.summary: The Government could rebate ABSD to owners of both a private property and an HDB flat who sell the HDB flat, prospectively affecting only future private property purchases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For those who are already concurrently owning both a private property and an HDB flat, the Government could incentivise them to sell their HDB flat by rebating the ABSD they paid at the time they purchased their private property if they choose to sell their HDB flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This would encourage private property owners to free up their HDB flats for others who cannot afford to buy private property.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This policy should be prospective so that it will not compel current HDB and private property owners to dispose of any property.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It will only affect those who currently own an HDB flat and decide to purchase a private property after the policy takes effect.

sections.label: HDB mission and housing affordability
sections.summary: The passage states that conflating two objectives will make housing more unaffordable for future generations and calls for focusing on HDB's original mission of quality, affordable housing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The longer we allow these two objectives to be conflated, the more unaffordable housing will become for future generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is time that we stopped kicking the can down the road and focus on HDB's original mission of providing quality and affordable housing for all Singaporeans, especially the lower- and middle-income earners.

sections.label: HDB home ownership goal
sections.summary: HDB aims to encourage home ownership through affordable, accessible public housing, with 80% of Singapore's population in HDB flats and about 90% owning them.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Since its inception, HDB's goal has been to encourage home ownership by making public housing affordable and accessible.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We can see that this has come to fruition as 80% of Singapore's population currently reside in HDB flats, of which about 90% own them.

sections.label: Group of HDB flat owners
sections.summary: The group made up 3.3% of all HDB flat owners, and about 45% of them rented out their whole flat.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In response, it was found that the group made up 3.3% of all HDB flat owners.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the subsequent sitting, it was mentioned that about 45% of this group are not living in their HDB flats as they have rented out their whole flat.

sections.label: Tengah BTO site productivity
sections.summary: BTOs at Tengah are expected to yield a 25% improvement in site productivity compared with other BTO projects.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, the BTOs at Tengah are expected to yield a 25% improvement in site productivity compared with other BTO projects.

sections.label: Changing stance on land cost
sections.summary: He changed his stance three times in three months on including land cost in HDB flat prices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, he said that we should not include the cost of the land into the prices of HDB flats; then he said we should use historical prices; yesterday he said that we could include the land cost, but delay it until we sell, and give it back to HDB together with interests.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Within three months, he changed his stance three times.

sections.label: CPF and flat price gap
sections.summary: People need not spend CPF money to buy a flat, but this will further increase the price gap between BTO and resale flats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Hence, people do not need to spend their CPF money to buy a flat.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, if you think twice, you will realise that this will further increase the price gap between BTO flats and resale flats.

sections.label: Stepping up BTO supply
sections.summary: The Government is right to step up BTO flat supply and give young couples priority through targeted measures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To resolve the current issue, I think the Government is right to step up the supply of BTO flats and give young couples priority to get a flat through targeted measures.

sections.label: Facebook post on land cost
sections.summary: Minister Desmond Lee referred to the speaker's 8 December 2022 Facebook post saying land cost should be taken out of the picture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Minister Desmond Lee referred to the Facebook post that I make on 8 December 2022, where I said "land cost should be taken out of the picture because much of the land used for building HDB flats were surrendered by the Pioneer Generation to the Government for a relatively modest sum under the Land Acquisition Act, between 1970s and 1980s." This is also in the Hansard.

sections.label: AHS and land cost
sections.summary: AHS takes land cost out of the picture for owner-occupation buyers, and the speaker rejects flip-flopping allegations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: AHS takes land cost out of the picture for people who buy flats for owner-occupation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: I have not pursued the matter up to now because I want to focus on the substance of the debate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: But I categorically reject allegations that I have been flip-flopping or made any proposal that HDB flats should be based on the historical cost of land.

sections.label: State land as reserves
sections.summary: The speaker says reserves are not just money, and state land also forms part of the reserves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: What I am saying is that reserves are not just money; state land also forms part of our reserves.

sections.label: Median BTO flat prices
sections.summary: Minister Desmond Lee's charts showed the average price of a 4-room BTO flat in a non-mature estate kept at $342,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Minister Desmond Lee has shown that the median prices in his charts yesterday, the average price of a 4-room BTO flat in a non-mature estate is kept at $342,000.

sections.label: HDB profit margin
sections.summary: HDB does not apply a profit margin on costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: HDB does not apply a profit margin on costs.

sections.label: Deficit under MND budget
sections.summary: Buyers pay HDB much less than land plus construction cost, and the deficit is made up under the MND budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Today, the amount buyers pay HDB is much less than land cost plus construction cost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The deficit is made up under the MND budget.

sections.label: HDB involvement in private market
sections.summary: A question asks why HDB wants to be involved in the private market sector if not to provide home ownership to Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Why does HDB want to be involved in the private market sector if it is not to provide home ownership to Singaporeans?

sections.label: HDB residents not condemned
sections.summary: Eighty percent of Singaporeans live in HDB flats, and the speaker says Singaporeans living in HDB flats should never be called condemned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Eighty percent of Singaporeans live in these HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Like Ms Carrie Tan who spoke before me, I was aghast to read that in a reply to a comment by someone on Facebook querying PSP's scheme, Mr Leong Mun Wai said that PSP's scheme was needed so that Singaporeans are not condemned to living in HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I am certainly glad that Mr Leong Mun Wai made a correction earlier on but I just want to say 80% of Singaporeans live in HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
