sentences.text: We should not – never – say that Singaporeans who live in HDB flats are condemned.

sections.label: Cannot afford, do not buy
sections.summary: The speaker says Mr Lim Biow Chuan will answer and that conceptually, if you cannot afford, you simply do not buy.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: I will let Mr Lim Biow Chuan answer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: I think conceptually, one must understand that if you cannot afford, then you simply do not buy.

sections.label: Options for low-income buyers
sections.summary: A speaker says those who cannot afford a flat can stay with parents or rent from HDB, and many applying for BTO flats suggests affordability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: If I am not able to afford a 3-room flat or 4-room flat because my income is very low, then I will look at options like staying with my parents, I will look at applying to HDB to rent a flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: But the fact that many of them apply to buy a BTO flat suggests that they are affordable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: There are so many schemes that the Government has put out to make these flats affordable.

sections.label: Affordable Homes Scheme inheritance
sections.summary: Under the Affordable Homes Scheme, if the original buyer passes away and leaves the flat to his children, they need not return land cost then.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   According this 安居乐 scheme (Affordable Homes Scheme), if the original buyer of the flat passes away and leaves the flat to his children, his children do not need to return the land cost at that point of time.

sections.label: Home ownership index comparison
sections.summary: The 2022 Urban Land Institute Asia Pacific Home Attainability Index lists home ownership as about 40% in Tokyo, 51% in Hong Kong, 64% in New South Wales and 88.9% in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: According to the 2022 Urban Land Institute Asia Pacific Home Attainability Index, home ownership in Tokyo is around 40%, around 51% in Hong Kong, 64% in New South Wales and 88.9% in Singapore.

sections.label: HDB resale and BTO statistics
sections.summary: The passage states that million-dollar HDB resale flats are around 1% of resale transactions and under 2% of first-time applicants took more than five BTO tries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In this debate, we will hear that the average percentage of monthly income that does towards housing payments averages at about 25% when in other cities, mortgages could be 40% to 50%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, what may be remembered outside of these Chambers are the stories of the few million-dollar resale HDBs or how a couple tried six times to apply for a BTO in a mature estate, even though factually, HDB resale flats that have been sold for over $1 million dollars make up a minority – around 1% of all HDB resale transactions in the past five years as of 2022 – and when statistics show that less than 2% of first-time applicants took more than five tries to get a BTO flat in a mature estate between 2019 and 2021.

sections.label: HDB ramping up BTO supply
sections.summary: HDB has committed to ramping up the supply of BTO flats, with some projects in mature estates, to meet strong public housing demand.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To meet the strong demand for public housing, HDB has already committed to ramping up the supply of BTO flats, with some of these projects being placed in mature estates.

sections.label: Stage of life housing grant proposal
sections.summary: The passage proposes a stage of life housing grant to encourage right-sizing first homes and lowering the MOP for 3-room flats to three years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Introduce a stage of life housing grant designed to motivate Singaporeans to right-size our first homes and mortgages at the start of our home ownership journey and increase the supply of potential 3-room flats available in the resale market by adjusting the Minimum Occupation Period (MOP) for such units downwards to three years.

sections.label: Grant for 4-room resale
sections.summary: After means testing, a couple could be eligible for the stage of life housing grant to further subsidise the cost of the 4-room resale.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: After means testing, such a couple could be eligible for stage of life housing grant, which will help to further subsidise the cost of the 4-room resale.

sections.label: Three generational flats in BTO
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government could consider making three generational flats a key feature of every BTO launch in mature estates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For BTO launches in mature estates, could the Government consider making three generational flats a key feature of every launch?

sections.label: Housing cash vouchers for PPHS
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government could consider an initiative to distribute housing cash vouchers for low-income families or PPHS renters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As part of the programme to help low-income families, or those who wish to rent a flat through the PPHS scheme, can the Government consider an initiative to distribute housing cash vouchers?

sections.label: Rental families buying homes
sections.summary: The speaker commends Government efforts and notes over 700 rental flat families bought their own homes in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I commend the Government's efforts and commitment to support Singaporeans' aspirations to own their own homes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am glad to read that over 700 families living in rental flats were able to buy their own homes in 2022.

sections.label: Forward Singapore and HDB land cost
sections.summary: The speaker supports Forward Singapore and recounts Mr Leong's Facebook posts arguing land cost be removed from HDB flat pricing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Government's efforts on Forward Singapore are in the right spirit and I urge more Singaporeans to come forward to the table for this direct opportunity for consultation and co-creation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Housing is a part of the Singapore dream, which must continue to be within the reach of each generation, so that our people feel like they have a home here and a tangible stake in our Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On a 8 December Facebook post, Mr Leong said, "in my opinion, the pricing of HDB flats should only account for construction costs and price differences between locations." He then said, "land cost should be taken out of the picture because much of the land use for building HDB flats were surrendered by the Pioneer Generation to the Government etc." On the 20 January, Mr Leong wrote again on Facebook, "it should be quite evident to Singaporeans that I am arguing for land cost to be taken out of the pricing of HDB flats", but in the current Affordable Homes Scheme that Mr Leong is proposing, the cost of land would be recorded and interests applied.

sections.label: Land cost for owner-occupation
sections.summary: The speaker says removing land cost means for owner-occupation, and sees no conflict with his Facebook idea.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: If you try to second-guess what my policy is and you fail to second-guess my policy, it is your problem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: So, when I say the land cost should be taken out of the picture, I mean, it should be taken out of the picture for owner-occupation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: And you did not guess that I actually have a second part to it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: So, there is no conflict in my first idea that I put up on Facebook and what I actually proposed in my speech yesterday.

sections.label: HDB building programme and BTO prices
sections.summary: HDB is catching up on building despite COVID-19, will launch up to 100,000 flats from 2021 to 2025, and kept BTO prices almost flat.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Despite the disruptions caused by COVID-19, HDB has been catching up on its building programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We will launch up to 100,000 flats between 2021 to 2025, if required.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The Government has also kept BTO prices almost flat, despite escalating construction costs, in order to ensure that flats remain affordable.

sections.label: Grant reduces Yishun flat price
sections.summary: A housing grant would reduce a Vanda Breeze @ Yishun 3-room flat's price from $200,000 to $130,000, about 4.3 times annual income.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: If they were to buy a 3-room flat in Vanda Breeze @ Yishun in the November 2022 BTO exercise, where the typical selling price was $200,000, the housing grant would reduce the selling price to $130,000, or about 4.3 times of their annual income.

sections.label: ComLink Rental Scheme support
sections.summary: The goal is stability, self-reliance and social mobility, with the ComLink Rental Scheme auto-enrolling eligible families with young children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Ultimately, our goal is to help these families achieve stability, self-reliance and eventually, social mobility.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: This is why we have gone further upstream to pair rental housing with ComLink to provide holistic social support for families entering rental housing, With the ComLink Rental Scheme we launched in November 2022, eligible families with young children will be automatically enrolled in ComLink when they apply to HDB for a public rental flat, even before they move in.

sections.label: HST rental households reached
sections.summary: Since it was set up in end 2019, the HST has reached out to about 1,400 rental households.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Since it was set up in end 2019, the HST has reached out to about 1,400 rental households.

sections.label: Fresh Start scheme enhancements
sections.summary: The scheme was enhanced last year by increasing the grant from $35,000 to $50,000, and from the February 2023 BTO exercise Fresh Start families can buy a 3-room flat on a shorter lease.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: This was also shared by Member of Parliament Nadia earlier.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We have just enhanced the scheme last year by increasing the grant amount from $35,000 to $50,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Starting from the February 2023 BTO exercise, Fresh Start families can also buy a 3-room flat on a shorter lease.

sections.label: Rental households awaiting keys
sections.summary: Another 2,300 rental households have booked a sold flat and are now waiting to collect their keys.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Another 2,300 rental households have booked a sold flat and are now waiting to collect their keys.

sections.label: Senior housing and monetisation options
sections.summary: Options for seniors include the Lease Buyback Scheme and Silver Housing Bonus, the EASE Programme introduced in 2012, HIP and EASE benefiting about 280,000 households, and Community Care Apartments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: For seniors who want to monetise their flats to support their retirement needs, we have various options available, such as the Lease Buyback Scheme and the Silver Housing Bonus.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: For example, we introduced the Enhancement for Active Seniors (EASE) Programme in 2012, more than 10 years ago.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: So far, about 280,000 households have benefited from HDB’s Home Improvement Programme (HIP) and EASE Programme, to make their homes more senior-friendly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Most recently, we introduced the Community Care Apartments, or CCAs in short, a new type of HDB flats that pairs senior-friendly housing with care services which can be personalised to seniors’ needs as they age.

sections.label: 2-room Flexi flat supply
sections.summary: The supply of 2-room Flexi flats has been ramped up from about 1,500 launched in 2013 to around 4,000 launched every year since 2014.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Mr Gerald Giam will be glad to know that we have been significantly ramping up the supply of 2-room Flexi flats from about 1,500 2-room Flexi flats launched in 2013 to around 4,000 such flats launched every year since 2014.

sections.label: Shortening BTO waiting times
sections.summary: Waiting times for BTO flats need to be shortened, and HDB should continue working with the construction sector on faster building techniques such as PPVC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: First and foremost, we need to shorten the waiting times for BTO Flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: HDB should continue to work with the construction sector on new and faster building techniques such as Prefabricated Prefinished Volumetric Construction, or PPVC method, to reduce time for completion of projects.

sections.label: Reviewing existing priority schemes
sections.summary: Existing priority schemes should be regularly reviewed and calibrated to prevailing demand, considering demographics and existing supply conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Existing priority schemes should be regularly reviewed and calibrated to suit prevailing demand requirements, giving consideration to demographics and existing supply conditions.

sections.label: Varying lease durations and pricing
sections.summary: HDB could review assigning leases of varying durations and pricing to improve affordability for first-timers wanting to stay near parents in mature estate BTO flats in central locations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Perhaps HDB can review the suitability of assigning leases of varying durations and pricing to augment the affordability to first-timers who really need to or want to stay close to their parents in mature estate BTO flats that are in central locations.

sections.label: HDB's 1960 establishment
sections.summary: The setting up of HDB in February 1960 expressed a commitment to provide affordable housing to the citizen population.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The setting up of HDB in February 1960 was an expression of a commitment to provide affordable housing to the citizen population.

sections.label: HDB housing record and CPF
sections.summary: HDB relieved the acute housing shortage within five years, and about 80% of residents live in public housing, with CPF a key pillar.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Within five years of its establishment, the Housing Development Board was able to relieve the acute housing shortage in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Now, 10 years after its formation is completed, more than 100,000 units of flats which provide homes for about 30% of the population, indeed a record of which Singapore can be proud." Today, as Members have cited, about 80% of Singapore's resident population live in public housing, of which about 90% own their flats.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A key pillar of the Government's record in providing affordable public housing to its citizens is the Central Provident Fund (CPF).

sections.label: Downsizing options for seniors
sections.summary: As they age, they can downsize to a smaller HDB flat, a 2-room flexi flat, a community care apartment with a shorter lease, or join the Lease Buyback Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They can downsize to a smaller HDB flat as they age.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They can move to a 2-room flexi flat or community care apartment with a shorter lease or join the Lease Buyback Scheme.

sections.label: Determining housing affordability
sections.summary: To determine housing affordability, HDB looks at buyers' household incomes and selling prices on Built-To-Order flats.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To determine housing affordability, the HDB looks at buyers' household incomes and selling prices on Built-To-Order (BTO) flats.

sections.label: Mortgage servicing ratio affordability
sections.summary: The MSR, the ratio of monthly mortgage payment to gross monthly household income, has remained below 25%, especially for smaller flats with lower median household incomes.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Another measure of housing affordability is the mortgage servicing ratio (MSR), which is the ratio of monthly mortgage payment to gross monthly household income expressed in percentage.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The MSR, as has been noted, has remained below 25% and has been lower than 25%, particularly for purchases of smaller flats with lower median household incomes.

sections.label: Workfare Income Supplement scheme
sections.summary: In the 2000s, the Government made the Workfare Income Supplement scheme a permanent part of Singapore's social safety net.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In response, in the 2000s, the Government made the Workfare Income Supplement scheme a permanent fixture of Singapore's social safety net.

sections.label: Stable employment and public housing
sections.summary: Stable employment is a precondition for keeping public housing affordable and accessible, and a 1968 CPF Act amendment allowed CPF savings for public housing purchases.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Having stable employment is a pertinent precondition for achieving the Government's goal of keeping public housing affordable and accessible for future generations of Singaporeans because history matters and our achieving the high ownership of housing came along with a CPF system, which we pretty much also inherited from the colonial administration.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is because studies of how Singapore has managed to achieve such high rates of ownership of public housing by Singaporeans point to September 1968, when an amendment to the CPF Act introduced the public housing scheme to allow members' CPF savings to be used to purchase public housing.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Drawing down on our past reserves to fund the enhanced Jobs Support Scheme enabled the Singapore economy to avoid a massive loss of jobs to retrenchment during the pandemic.

sections.label: Affordable Homes Scheme land cost
sections.summary: Mr Leong Mun Wai's proposed Affordable Homes Scheme would have BTO purchasers who live in their units until lease end pay a price excluding land cost.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the Motion standing in the name of Mr Leong Mun Wai, a proposed scheme dubbed the Affordable Homes Scheme, if I understand it correctly, has the feature that have purchasers of BTO flats who subsequently live in their units until the end of their lease pay a price that does not factor in the land cost.

sections.label: Proposed scheme and past reserves
sections.summary: The proposed scheme may mean a huge financial outlay for sellers and would leave smaller past reserves to draw on during economic storms.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This, I think as noted by some Members as well already, may involve a huge financial outlay for the individual seller, especially if the recovery of total land cost is applied only to sellers after the minimum occupation period, which would deter resale.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, in sum total, under the proposed scheme, the size of past reserves that can be drawn upon during big storms that hit the Singapore economy will be smaller compared to the current system.

sections.label: Economic inclusion and housing affordability
sections.summary: The journey ahead is more challenging as aspirations rise and growth room diminishes, but focusing on economic inclusion through affordable housing and growth provides hope.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck
sentences.text: The journey ahead, however, is likely to be more challenging as citizens' aspirations are now higher and the room for growth spurts diminishes in a mature economy.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck
sentences.text: Nevertheless, keeping a focus on achieving economic inclusion through providing affordable and accessible housing while continuing to grow the economic pie through innovation and productivity increases to raise tax revenues to fund housing grants provides hope that the well-being of the current and future generations of Singaporeans can be further improved.

sections.label: 2-room Flexi flat demand
sections.summary: Member asks if HDB plans to increase 2-room Flexi flats given demand exceeds supply and about 71,000 senior households may want to right-size.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: During my speech, I shared that the demand for these flats still exceeds the supply by quite a bit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And given that our population is ageing and there are, by my calculations, about 71,000 senior households that potentially would want to right-size their flats, does HDB plan to further increase the number of 2-room Flexi flats in the coming years, and if so, by how much?

sections.label: Watching ageing demand
sections.summary: The speaker assures the Member that they are watching this carefully and planning to do a lot more as ageing comes in big waves.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: I want to assure the Member that we are watching this carefully.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We are also planning to do a lot more, because ageing is coming in big waves.

sections.label: BTO affordability ratios
sections.summary: Annex 2 shows HPI for 2-room, 3-room and 4-room BTO flats in non-mature estates stayed below five since 2015, and close to 70% of 2022 launches are affordable at $8,400 income.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Annex 2 shows how the House Price to Income ratio (HPI) for 2-room, 3-room and 4-room BTO flats in non-mature estates have remained below five since 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Close to 70% of the BTO flats launched in 2022 across all estates, can be affordably purchased with a household income of $8,400 at a Mortgage Servicing Ratio of 25% or less, meaning that these households use a quarter or less of their household income to pay for the mortgage instalments.

sections.label: Building programme and waiting times
sections.summary: Building fell behind in the last three years due to COVID-19; up to 100,000 new flats will be launched between 2021 and 2025, with median waiting time to fall to three to four years from 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Our building programme fell behind in the last three years due to COVID-19, we are catching up and are committed to launch up to 100,000 new flats between 2021 and 2025, if needed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The median waiting time is now four to four and a half years, and we are working to bring this down to three to four years from 2024.

sections.label: Affordable Homes Scheme sustainability
sections.summary: Members cited fiscal sustainability concerns, and the prominent element in Mr Leong's proposed Affordable Homes Scheme does not quite meet the test of sustainability.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Many Members, including Members from the Opposition, have cited fiscal sustainability concerns and we are very glad to see convergence on this important issue.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: But this prominent element in the "Affordable Homes Scheme" (AHS), which Mr Leong proposed, does not quite meet the test of sustainability.

sections.label: HDB land cost
sections.summary: HDB must pay for the cost of land used to build flats, and it is incorrect to treat that land like land for public infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: HDB must pay for the cost of the land used to build flats.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: It is simply incorrect to say that the land on which HDB flats are built should be treated like the land on which public infrastructure is built.

sections.label: Subsidised rental housing targeting
sections.summary: Subsidised rental housing is kept very targeted for families who cannot afford home ownership, despite sympathy for young people's needs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We are sympathetic to the aspirations and diverse needs of our young.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: But we have good reasons for keeping subsidised rental housing very targeted, for families who cannot afford home ownership.

sections.label: HDB loans for resale flats
sections.summary: HDB loans for resale flats are provided based on the market valuation of the actual resale flats instead of the posted price of new flats.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Instead of giving out HDB loans for resale based on the posted price of new flats, we began to provide HDB loans based on the market valuation of the actual resale flats.

sections.label: Loan tenure and CPF payouts
sections.summary: Fully paid loans averaged 17 years against original tenure of 23 years, and about eight in 10 active CPF members turning 55 in 2027 can set aside at least the BRS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The average tenure for those who have fully paid up their loans is 17 years, while their average original loan tenure was 23 years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Today, we expect about eight in 10 active CPF members turning 55 in 2027 to be able to set aside at least the BRS in their Retirement Account and hence, receive the corresponding BRS payout or more.

sections.label: Flat lease and CPF usage
sections.summary: Policies were refined so Singaporeans are less likely to outlive their flat lease without a significant CPF LIFE payout, with CPF usage and HDB loan pro-rated for shorter leases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the fact that 99% of those owning a HDB flat now can live in it till age 95 or more, we recently refined our policies to make it even less likely that a Singaporean would outlive the lease of his flat while also not having a significant CPF LIFE payout.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Those purchasing a flat whose lease can last them till age 95 can obtain the maximum CPF usage and HDB housing loan, while those buying flats with shorter leases would have CPF utilisation and HDB loan amount pro-rated.

sections.label: Resale flat asset appreciation
sections.summary: A 30-year-old who bought the flat on the resale market in 2023 can see asset appreciation over his lifetime.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: I am pretty sure he drew it to scale.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: And 60 years, that means a 30-year-old who bought this flat on the resale market in 2023 can see asset appreciation over his lifetime.

sections.label: First-timer BTO buyers' MSR
sections.summary: Nine in 10 first-timer BTO buyers who collected keys to non-mature estate flats in 2022 had an MSR of 25% or less and could service their loan fully with CPF, without cash.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Nine in 10 first-timer BTO flat buyers who collected their keys to non-mature estate flats in 2022 had an MSR of 25% or less and could service their loan fully with CPF, without cash.

sections.label: Projected revenue and GST increase
sections.summary: Projections show more than $2.3 billion per year, exceeding the value of a 1% GST increase.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Based on our projections, it comes up to more than $2.3 billion per year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: If our Members are curious as to what this means in terms of additional revenue that has to be raised through taxes, this is more than the value of the 1% increase in GST.

sections.label: HDB flat affordability and accessibility
sections.summary: HDB has ensured affordability and accessibility of flats, building faster than HDB population growth while keeping affordability targets.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Minister Desmond Lee has made clear in his speech yesterday that HDB has ensured the affordability and accessibility of flats, especially that of BTO units in non-mature estates.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We have been building HDB flats at a faster rate than HDB residential population growth, while generally keeping to affordability targets.

sections.label: CPF LIFE payouts without monetising flat
sections.summary: Homeowners can receive lifelong CPF LIFE payouts without monetising their flat; eight in 10 active members turning 55 in 2027 can set aside BRS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Even if the homeowner does not monetise or sell his flat, he can still receive lifelong monthly cash payouts through CPF LIFE.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: It is estimated that eight in every 10 active CPF members turning 55 in 2027 will be able to set aside the Basic Retirement Sum (BRS) and receive the corresponding BRS payout, and this is without having to monetise their HDB flat.

sections.label: 99-year lease and home value
sections.summary: The Government states 99 years means 99 years, home value falls to zero eventually, but 99 years covers a buyer's lifetime.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The Government would never mislead the public. 99 years means 99 years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: It is common knowledge that home value will fall to zero when the time eventually comes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: But 99 years is a very long time for a flat buyer, sufficient to cover his lifetime.

sections.label: Flat leases and appreciating asset
sections.summary: If buyers avoid flats with too-short leases, they can enjoy an appreciating asset over their lifetime, with policies restricting CPF use for shorter leases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: As long as flat buyers do not buy flats whose leases are too short, it is entirely possible to enjoy the benefits of an appreciating asset throughout their lifetime.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The Government has already thought of this and adjusted our policies in recent years, putting in place more restrictions in the use of CPF to buy flats with shorter leases, to make such situations less likely.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Hence, the same flat is very likely to bring the benefits of an appreciating asset to the flat owner over his lifetime and to an extent, part of his children's lifetime, although certainly not his grandchildren's lifetime.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: However, the flat owner's children and grandchildren can buy their own flats and, with support from Government policies, benefit from the appreciation of their own assets.

sections.label: Land pricing approaches
sections.summary: The speaker said doing so was one approach and suggested another favoured by the Workers' Party: pricing land after setting a target multiple of new home owners' salaries.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Just to clear, what I had said was that doing so was but one approach.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I even suggested a different approach, which the Workers' Party favours – that land be priced after setting a target multiple of new home owners' salaries.

sections.label: Government as purchaser of last resort
sections.summary: The Government acts as purchaser of last resort for flat owners' remaining lease value, and would not offer VERS if the private market would do it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The Government comes in as the purchaser of last resort, when no one else would actually purchase and give the flat owner the remaining value of the lease.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Well, if the Government thought that the private market would do it, we would not be offering VERS.

sections.label: Opportunity cost of real estate investment
sections.summary: The speaker clarifies he meant the opportunity cost of investing too much in real estate, foregoing higher-return assets such as equities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: I was not talking about the opportunity cost of retirement time, for which I am sure we all have plans.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: But rather the opportunity cost of investing too much in real estate and thereby foregoing investment in other higher-return assets, such as equities, for instance, which in general have higher returns than real estate.

sections.label: Clarification on VERS for all HDB blocks
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Senior Minister of State whether the Government will offer VERS to all blocks of HDB flats in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: I initially did not want any clarification, but since the Senior Minister of State brought up VERS, I thought I would just ask one point of clarification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: I think the Senior Minister of State has affirmed the important role that VERS is playing within this whole ecosystem of housing policies, as she alluded to, if I understand her correctly, to sort of backstop the resale prices from plunging too catastrophically when they get past year 60.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: So, can I clarify with the Senior Minister of State if the Government going to offer VERS to all blocks of HDB flats in Singapore?

sections.label: Reaction to HPI charts
sections.summary: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim and Mr Leon Perera were reacting to charts Minister Desmond Lee showed about HPI of 5 for non-mature estate flats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim and I think, Mr Leon Perera, I believe they were reacting to the charts that Minister Desmond Lee showed yesterday which was about HPI of 5 and that is for non-mature estate flats.

sections.label: Affordability peg and buyer preferences
sections.summary: The speaker says no number is naturally compelling for pegging affordability, judgment is involved, and buyers prefer lower prices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: To the Leader of Opposition, I was referring to the fact that currently, what we have shown is that we have kept to 5 and in the context of your Members asking: how about 3 – how about considering 3, I was trying to explain that it is not to say that there is any number that is naturally compelling, but that if we are talking about how to peg affordability, I think there is some judgment involved, and I think to buyers, we understand that to buyers, lower prices would always be more preferred and more welcomed.

sections.label: BTO pricing and MSR policy
sections.summary: BTO prices are pegged to around 25% MSR of applicant's income rather than market price, with grants for first-timers and unchanged HDB loan rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In fact, the current policy not to peg the BTO prices to the market price but at around 25% mortgage servicing ratio (MSR) of the applicant's income is better, with additional grants to first-timers to ensure that the flats are within their reach and the price of BTO is based on income and not market price.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The 25% MSR is lower than the international affordability guideline of 30% to 35% MSR.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In addition, residents are grateful that HDB has been working with CPF to keep the HDB housing loan rates unchanged despite that the market interest rate has been rising for the past one year.

sections.label: Property tax and first-timer grants
sections.summary: The Government may need to review seller profit taxes and increase first-timer grants alongside supply to check runaway prices while supporting first-timer home ownership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This will require the Government to continually look into further regulation and cooling measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I would suggest that the Government may need to review the tax on profits made by the sellers of property and HDB flats and increase the grants to first-timers in additional to increase in supply to achieve both objectives to check on runaway prices without fundamentals while supporting our first-timer Singaporeans to own their home.

sections.label: Core BTO problems
sections.summary: The core problem is not overall BTO affordability but BTO shortage, long waiting times, a shifting BTO mix, and high resale prices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Because, and this is why I am rather bemused by the more far-reaching proposals to bring BTO prices down, the core problem today is not overall BTO affordability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The real issues to solve today are: (a) BTO shortage and long waiting times, driven by, as we have said, COVID-19 disruptions and construction delays; (b) a shifting BTO mix with a higher proportion of BTOs in mature estates against expectations of home buyers; and (c) high resale prices partly driven by the supply-demand imbalance which is itself partially real, partially induced, partly by nearly a decade of low interest rates.

sections.label: Woodlands and Bukit Merah application rates
sections.summary: In the August 2022 Woodlands launch, application rates were 8.1 and 11.7 per unit for 3- and 4-room flats versus 2.7 and 6.1 for Bukit Merah PLH BTOs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In the last BTO launch in Woodlands in August 2022, Woodlands South Plains, the application rate was 8.1 and 11.7 applicants per unit for 3- and 4-room flats respectively versus 2.7 and 6.1 for the Bukit Merah PLH BTOs.

sections.label: BTO fairness and incentives
sections.summary: Because BTOs are such a good deal, everyone wants to jump in, making it a fairness and incentives issue, not just affordability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Plus, because BTOs are such a good deal, everyone wants to jump in.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, it is not just a housing affordability issue; it becomes a fairness issue and an incentives issue.

sections.label: Number of HDB flats and households
sections.summary: There are currently approximately 1.1 million HDB flats, meaning 1.1 million HDB households for which the flat is a significant part of their wealth.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But first allow me to lay down one fact.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There are currently approximately 1.1 million HDB flats; and that means 1.1 million HDB households for which their flat represents a significant part of their wealth.

sections.label: Calibrated resale and BTO measures
sections.summary: The resale market must be part of the solution, and if it is a bubble, air should be taken out bit by bit through calibrated measures in both markets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, the resale market has to be part of the solution.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But if the market is a bubble, the more responsible way is to take some of the air out, bit by bit, through carefully calibrated measures acting in concert, in both the BTO and the resale market.

sections.label: Safety stock of flats
sections.summary: Building surplus flats has a financial cost, but social benefits and housing delay costs may justify a safety stock of readily-available flats alongside BTO and SWT flats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There is a financial cost to building what is effectively surplus flats to the demand forecasted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But if we really take into account the social benefit of housing and the cost of housing delays, there is potential merit in maintaining a safety stock of readily-available or some might say, Zero Waiting Time flats, while maintaining a baseload of BTO and SWT flats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: A further suggestion for the BTO market that seems worthy of further consideration is building shorter tenure flats, say 50 years as in the case of the Ang Mo Kio SERS replacement flats.

sections.label: Proximity Grant increase
sections.summary: The Proximity Grant for first-time buyers in areas with high BTO application rates should be increased.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: First, to increase the Proximity Grant for first-time buyers in areas with high BTO application rates.

sections.label: HDB owners with private property
sections.summary: The Government could require HDB owners who own private property to sell their flats; about 30,000 HDB owners own at least one private property.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In fact, if a stronger signal needs to be sent, the Government could consider additionally requiring HDB owners who own private property today to sell their flats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Three percent of HDB owners, slightly over 30,000 HDB owners own at least one private property.

sections.label: Singaporean household home ownership
sections.summary: 95% of Singaporean households are home owners today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Today, 95% of Singaporean households are home owners.

sections.label: BTO waiting time and resale prices
sections.summary: Two main concerns are BTO waiting time and resale flat prices, and new BTO flats are affordable if buyers choose affordable locations with or without grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Their two main concerns are the waiting time for BTO flats and the price of resale flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: From my exchange with them, we acknowledge that new BTO flats are affordable as long as buyers choose locations that they can afford, with or without opting to utilise the available grants.

sections.label: Grants for new and resale flats
sections.summary: Government grants of up to $80,000 for new flats and up to $160,000 for resale flats are available where applicable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Government grants of up to $80,000 for new flats while generous amount of up to $160,000 for resale flats are also available where applicable.

sections.label: Housing prices and grants
sections.summary: People have expressed concern over rising housing prices, but housing grants are available to the people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Lately, we have heard many people expressing their concern over housing prices that keep increasing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, we should acknowledge that there are housing grants being made available to the people.

sections.label: Support for public housing Motion
sections.summary: Public housing policies have helped thousands of families own a home within their means, and the speaker supports the Motion affirming public housing is affordable and accessible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (In English): Sir, our home is a place to stay and also an asset for our golden years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We have to acknowledge that public housing policies have helped thousands of families to own a house of their own as long as they choose a size and location that is within their financial means.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This, in my view, is the correct approach to take as it strikes a nice balance between ensuring the public housing is affordable from the Government's end while encouraging Singaporeans to save and spend prudently within their means as responsible citizens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On this note, I hereby strongly support this Motion by Minister Desmond Lee to affirm that public housing is affordable and accessible for our Singaporeans.

sections.label: PSP's Affordable Homes Scheme
sections.summary: PSP's Motion rests on its proposal to change HDB's homeownership programme into a prepaid rental scheme with an option to buy.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: PSP's Motion rests upon – and its merits must therefore be judged by – their alternative policy proposal which, in essence, is to change the HDB's existing homeownership programme into a national prepaid rental scheme with an option to buy.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: PSP's proposal or, as Mr Leong Mun Wai calls it, the Affordable Homes Scheme, is in substance a prepaid rental scheme where the user pays rental upfront and has the option to own the flat by paying a deferred land cost.

sections.label: Three ways future generations pay
sections.summary: You, your children and grandchildren will pay through erosion of reserves, inequity, and poor policy affecting the housing market.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: You, your children and your grandchildren will pay for it in three ways: (a) financially, through the erosion of our shared reserves; (b) in inequity, where some benefit at the expense of others; and (c) in poor policy, with implications for the broader housing market.

sections.label: State land cannot be given free
sections.summary: The Government cannot give away state land for free or sell it at an under-value.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Government cannot give away state land for free or sell it at an under-value.

sections.label: Net Investment Return Contribution split
sections.summary: Fifty percent of investment returns supplements the national budget through NIRC, the other 50% is reinvested, and NIRC contributes $0.20 per dollar of expenditure.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Fifty percent of the investment returns supplement our national budget annually through the Net Investment Return Contribution (NIRC) and the other 50% is reinvested for the benefit of ourselves and future generations in a virtuous cycle.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Today, the NIRC contributes $0.20 for every dollar of expenditure.

sections.label: PSP proposal reserves effect
sections.summary: PSP's proposal would let new users benefit from low-cost flats while eroding reserves and reducing NIRC to the budget.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Ultimately, the net effect of PSP's proposal is that the new users will benefit from the low-cost flats but it would lead to the erosion of reserves and the reduction in NIRC to the budget.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In short, PSP's proposal will benefit the user but everyone else will be paying for it.

sections.label: HDB flat ownership versus rental
sections.summary: The PSP scheme shows PSP understands the distinction between rental and ownership, contrary to their social media posts.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: While on this topic, I also want to highlight one other thing.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: There is a narrative going about that you do not own your HDB flats and that you are only a tenant and paying rental.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Mr Leong asked in a social media post in December 2021, and I quote, "is the land used by HDB truly disposed of by the Government if the HDB flat owners only own the rights to their flat and not the common areas and amenities?" And he also said that "flat owners arguably paying a fixed monthly rent for 99 years in today's dollar upfront when they purchase their flat." In a social media post in July 2020, Mr Louis Chua said that "signing an agreement for lease makes one a lessee, not an owner".

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This scheme of PSP shows that that is not true.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: It shows that they fully understand that there is a distinction between rental and ownership.

sections.label: Support for Minister's Motion
sections.summary: The speaker cannot support PSP's Motion but supports the Minister for National Development's Motion.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For these reasons, I cannot support the PSP's Motion standing in the name of Mr Leong Mun Wai and Ms Hazel Poa, but I do support the Motion standing in the name of the Minister for National Development for all the reasons that have been outlined by the Minister.

sections.label: VERS voting and recourse
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether VERS is subject to precinct-level voting and what recourse a young family has if their precinct does not vote for it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And I think this is actually a key plank of what the Workers' Party (WP) has said in the Universal Sale and Lease Back Scheme which we put out, that the HDB is the buyer of last resort for all lessees, at the option of the lessee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But can I confirm that VERS is subject to voting on a precinct level and that it is far less generous than SERS?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: So, for a young family that buy, say, a Marine Parade flat today which has about 50 years left, the original owner would be able to monetise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But for this young family, should the precincts not actually vote for VERS, then, what recourse would he or she has, and does it mean that their home, or rather, their household net worth would be declining as a result of this.

sections.label: HDB flats and home ownership
sections.summary: 78.3% of Singapore resident households live in HDB flats, with over 1.09 million flats supplied and high home ownership rates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Outcome number one: 78.3% of Singapore resident households live in HDB flats, and today, HDB has supplied more than 1.09 million flats in Singapore, nine in 10 of which are owner-occupied, resulting in Singapore having one of the highest home ownership rates in the world.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And even more heartwarming to know is that 85% of low-income households in Singapore own and live in their own HDB flats.

sections.label: Buyers' MSR in 2022
sections.summary: In the first half of 2022, almost 90% of buyers collecting keys for new HDB flats had an MSR of 25% or lower.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the first half of 2022, almost 90% of all buyers who collected keys for their new HDB flats has a MSR of 25% or lower.

sections.label: HDB price-to-income ratio
sections.summary: In 2021, the median HDB flat price-to-income ratio was 4.5, about four and a half times median annual household income.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Outcome number four: in 2021, the median price-to-income ratio for HDB flats in Singapore was 4.5, which means that the median HDB flat price is about four and a half times the median annual household income in Singapore.

sections.label: BTO wait times
sections.summary: BTO flats have a median wait time of 4.3 years, and HDB is using a hybrid of build-ahead flats to shorten waits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Challenge number one is said many times, long wait time for BTO Flats with median wait time of 4.3 years, not counting the long queue to apply and book for a flat.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: HDB is already implementing a hybrid of Build-ahead a certain number of flats to compliment BTOs to shorten wait times.

sections.label: HDB flat affordability
sections.summary: HDB says flats exist for different incomes and needs, and BTO flats are priced to affordability, not cost recovery.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: HDB has assured that there is a HDB flat out there for a different range of incomes and needs, and that the BTO flat is priced to affordability and is not priced to recover cost.

sections.label: Resale market cooling measures
sections.summary: Government measures to cool the heated resale market have been introduced and will take time to work through the market.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government measures to cool the currently heated resale market have already been introduced and will take time to work through the market.

sections.label: HDB rental gains rules
sections.summary: It asks whether rules or caps exist on rental gains for this category of HDB owners and whether rent control ensures affordable rental housing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Are there any rules or caps on rental gains for this category of HDB owners?

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Is there any rent control to ensure that the rental prices of HDB rooms and HDB flats will provide affordable rental housing for our guest workers?

sections.label: Mdm T's Fresh Start journey
sections.summary: Mdm T moved into a rental flat in 2016, joined HDB's Fresh Start schemes, got a full-time job and an HDB flat.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: She moved into a rental flat with her children in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: She was emplaced in HDB's Fresh Start Housing Scheme (FSHS) in March 2020 and was referred to the Fresh Start Support Programme (FSSP) in July 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To cut a long story short, Mdm T, with the help of the FSSP social worker, managed to get a full-time job, moved into her HDB flat under the FSSH, got help from generous donors to set up her home, learnt to be more confident in planning, managing her children and is taking on the responsibility of managing her own bills and not burdening her mother and still have some savings left over.

sections.label: Land cost repayment on flat sales
sections.summary: PSP would not charge land cost at point of sale, but Singaporeans selling flats must repay full land costs plus interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: PSP would not charge land course at the point of sales, but when Singaporeans in sell their flats, they have to pay back the full costs of land plus interest.

sections.label: Four HDB housing measures
sections.summary: Four measures are suggested: extending the housing priority grant to a 30-minute public transport journey and reserving 30% of new BTOs in mature estates for extended proximity grant applicants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: To achieve that, let me suggest four measures: one, HDB can extend the housing priority grant beyond of families living within four kilometres of family members to also include those within a 30-minute off-peak journey by public transport, given that we have extended our MRT network considerably; two, HDB can reserve 30% of new BTOs in mature estates for applicants who qualify for the extended proximity grants which I just mentioned, the enhanced	proximity grants.

sections.label: Resale and private market impact
sections.summary: The resale HDB market will be devastated first, followed by the private property market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: The resale HDB market will be devastated first, followed by the private property market.

sections.label: Owners dumping flats for BTOs
sections.summary: Many existing HDB owners will dump their flats anticipating a sharp resale value drop, then apply for new BTOs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Right off the bat, many existing HDB owners will wise up and dump the existing flats in anticipation of the future sharp drop in resale value, and then apply for new BTOs.

sections.label: Interest rates and property prices
sections.summary: US and Singapore interest rates are much higher than two years ago, and a soft landing in property prices is needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Interest rates in the US and Singapore are much higher compared to two years ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: In fact, we have just gone through the fastest ever increase in interest rate in history.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Many developing countries are now seeing and experiencing a steep drop in housing prices at this juncture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: We must strive to achieve a soft landing in our property prices or for a price increase to be less than our increase in income.

sections.label: Finetuning BTO policies
sections.summary: MND should finetune policies to improve accessibility and affordability of new BTOs in attractive locations while avoiding sudden destabilising actions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: We are still trying to catch up on delayed BTO construction, so it is natural that some Singaporeans are anxious.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: But I hope that MND can focus on finetuning our policies to improve the accessibility and affordability of new BTOs in attractive locations while ensuring that we stay clear of sudden destabilising actions.

sections.label: Home Ownership for the People Scheme
sections.summary: In 1964 the Government introduced the Home Ownership for the People Scheme so Singaporeans would own rather than rent their flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 1964, the Government introduced the Home Ownership for the People Scheme so that Singaporeans would own rather than rent their flats.

sections.label: HDB resale and land acquisition
sections.summary: In 1971 the Government allowed HDB flats to be resold for a profit, and in 1973 a Land Acquisition Act amendment let the Government buy land at prices independent of purchase price or market rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 1971, there was a significant shake-up in public housing when the Government allowed HDB flats to be resold for a profit, although not investment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 1973, an amendment to the Land Acquisition Act allowed the Government to purchase land from owners at prices independent of the land's purchase price or prevailing market rates.

sections.label: Delinking HDB prices from resale prices
sections.summary: The then Minister for National Development Khaw Boon Wan announced the policy decision to delink HDB prices from resale prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To deal with that, the then Minister for National Development Khaw Boon Wan announced the policy decision to delink HDB prices from resale prices.

sections.label: Resale price increases and BTO supply
sections.summary: Resale prices rose because people need homes and HDB did not build enough BTOs to meet demand, and over five years 5-room and executive resale flats rose faster than 4-room flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Resale prices have increased because people need homes and the HDB did not build enough BTOs to meet demand, which should have been known and calculable, notwithstanding COVID-19 related delays.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Over the last five years, the prices of larger resale flat, specifically 5-room and executive flats, have risen even faster than 4-room resale flats.

sections.label: Taxpayer subsidy and HPI affordability
sections.summary: The house price to annual income is a common gauge of HDB flat affordability, but in Singapore the taxpayer subsidy keeps the number in check.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While the house price to annual income (HPI) is a common gauge to appreciate the affordability of HDB flats, in the Singapore context, it is the taxpayer subsidy, or what the Government refers to as generous subsidies, that is keeping the number in check.

sections.label: BTO waiting times
sections.summary: Today, waiting times can stretch up to four to five years for BTO flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Today, waiting times can stretch up to four to five years for BTO flats.

sections.label: Rental options and short-wait BTO flats
sections.summary: The passage proposes expanding rental options to 3-room or 4-room flats and notes only 8% of 2022 flats were short-wait BTO.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Other options include expanding rental options for low-income households, which host large families to flat types that can be up to 3-room or even 4-room in size.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I acknowledge the reply given by Minister Desmond Lee to Sengkang GRC Member of Parliament, Mr Louis Chua Kheng Wee by way of his Parliamentary Question that since 2018, the HDB has offered close to 11,000 BTO flats with shorter waiting times of less than three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, as the Minister revealed, for the 23,184 flats launched in 2022, only 8% are short-wait BTO flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Minister's new commitment, as announced yesterday, to increase this to 2,000 to 3,000 flats each year, will not move the 2022 figure of 8% in a significant way.

sections.label: Lowering flat prices and land costs
sections.summary: The passage states that increasing grants or removing land costs could lower prices, and that selling state land below market value requires the President's approval.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Other means of lowering prices could be to increase grants to first timers or take land costs out of prices and recover this when the flat is resold." In a POFMA clarification on 14 October 2022 directed at Yeoh Lam Keong by the Ministry of National Development, the Government stated that it cannot sell state land at nominal or at a much lower cost than its fair market value without the President's approval, as doing so would constitute a draw on past reserves.

sections.label: Waterway Banks project subsidies
sections.summary: The passage states the Waterway Banks project cost $279 million, sales proceeds were $240 million, and asks whether subsidies are applied equally across flat sizes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The project cost was $279 million and the sales proceeds amounted to $240 million with taxpayer subsidies making up to $39 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Coming back to Minister Khaw's revelation of subsidies from the Waterway Banks' project, will Minister Desmond Lee confirm if taxpayer subsidies to make up the difference between the sales proceeds and project costs are applied equally, regardless if a buyer purchased a 2-room or 4-room flat for example, or is the subsidy tiered proportionally to flat sizes?

sections.label: Subsidies for post-2006 BTO lessees
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister to clarify the range of subsidies received by 4-room mature and non-mature BTO lessees, given a fixed $40,000 resale levy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify, for individuals who bought a BTO flat after 3 March 2006, when there was a change in resale levy policy, what is the range of subsidies a 4-room mature and non-mature BTO flat lessee respectively would have received, even though the actual resale levy is fixed for both lessees at $40,000 by HDB?

sections.label: Workers' Party Motion amendment
sections.summary: The passage states that the Workers' Party proposes an amendment to the Motion in the Minister for National Development's name.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party proposes an amendment to the Motion in the name of the Minister for National Development.

sections.label: PAP Motion and BTO concerns
sections.summary: The passage states that voting for the PAP Motion would mean Singaporeans accept four-to-five-year waits and BTO prices such as $877,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Voting for the PAP Motion, as drafted originally by the Minister for National Development would mean that Singaporeans are satisfied with waiting up to four to five years for a HDB BTO flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: It would also mean that Singaporeans do not have quarrel or concern with the price of some BTO flats, such as 5-room BTO flats in Ang Mo Kio, priced at $877,000 and the significant increase in resale flat prices across the board recently.

sections.label: Amending Motion on HDB affordability
sections.summary: Amending the Motion to intensify efforts on affordable and accessible HDB flats would match Singaporeans' expectations for public housing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Amending the Motion to call on the Government to intensify its efforts to make HDB flats more affordable and accessible would be consistent with the reasonable expectations that Singaporeans have for public housing today.

sections.label: PSP proposals on land pricing
sections.summary: The PSP's proposals are separate from the Motion, and a deep conversation on land pricing policy should be a Government priority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: On the PSP's specific proposals which are separate from the wording of the Motion, we believe a deep conversation of the options surrounding land pricing policy and how land for public use is valued, should be a priority of the Government to ensure HDB flats can be more affordable and accessible, particularly in the face of the use of more taxpayer subsidies to fund the HDB home ownership programme.

sections.label: HDB home ownership rate
sections.summary: Today, 90% of Singaporean households own their HDB homes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Today, 90% of Singaporean households own their HDB homes.

sections.label: Ramping up HDB flat supply
sections.summary: The Government is ramping up supply, launching up to 100,000 new flats from 2021 to 2025 and more Shorter Waiting Time flats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We are taking active, concrete steps to resolve the imbalance and address the concerns that Singaporeans have raised.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We are decisively ramping up the housing supply and will launch up to a total of 100,000 new flats between 2021 and 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Members may recall that we announced this in 2021, in the midst of fighting COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We will also launch more Shorter Waiting Time flats, of around 2,000 to 3,000 flats per year by 2025, and we will recalibrate our building programme over time so that they make up a larger proportion of new flat supply, with flat supply comprising BTO flats, Shorter Waiting Time flats as part of BTO flat supply, Sale of Balance Flats and Open Booking of Flats, on top of the resale market options.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Mr Xie Yao Quan, Ms Denise Phua, Mr Louis Chua and Mr Leon Perera had called for building ahead of demand and building Shorter Waiting Time flats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We have priced BTO flats to ensure affordability and kept BTO prices stable in the last two years.

sections.label: Allocating resources for public housing
sections.summary: The Government will prioritise first-timer families and help lower-income households more, believing in housing as a social leveller.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: So, how do we allocate limited resources for public housing among potentially unlimited housing needs, while reflecting our values as a nation?

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We will prioritise first-timer families who need housing to build their families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We will help lower-income households more because we believe in housing as a social leveller.

sections.label: HDB flats under construction
sections.summary: Almost 80,000 HDB flats are under construction, and by about 2025 about 150 BTO projects are expected at the same time.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: There are almost 80,000 HDB flats under construction, as we speak.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: This high tempo will continue and by about 2025, we expect to have about 150 BTO projects going on at the same time.

sections.label: 31,000 unsold HDB flats
sections.summary: HDB ended up with 31,000 unsold flats, which took more than five years to clear.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: HDB ended up with 31,000 unsold flats, which took more than five years to clear.

sections.label: HDB flats launched 2018-2020
sections.summary: HDB launched around 16,000 flats in 2018, 15,000 in 2019 and 17,000 in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: To put this into context, HDB launched around 16,000 flats in 2018, the year before the report; 15,000 flats in 2019; and 17,000 flats in 2020.

sections.label: HPI and mortgage servicing ratios
sections.summary: HPI is less than three after grants for the 25th percentile, and in 2022 almost nine in 10 first-time BTO buyers had MSRs under 25%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: With this approach, today, HPI, or Home Price to Income ratio, is less than three after grants for those at the 25th percentile – or households at the bottom 25% in terms of total household income.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In 2022, almost nine in 10 first-time BTO flat buyers have mortgage servicing ratios (MSRs) of less than 25%.

sections.label: Example of 4-room BTO affordability
sections.summary: A family with $5,000 household income can receive $45,000 in grants and afford a $342,000 4-room BTO flat at 21% MSR.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: To give an example, using the average price of $342,000 for a 4-room BTO flat in a non-mature estate in 2022, a family with a household income of $5,000 can receive $45,000 in housing grants and affordably purchase the BTO flat at an MSR of 21%.

sections.label: Pricing flats by affordability indicators
sections.summary: Affordability indicators and mortgage servicing ratios determine pricing so buyers can afford flats, at prices lower than the resale market can bear.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Then, we determine the affordability indicators for different income levels, the mortgage servicing ratios, and we then know that we need to price it at a certain level so that buyers can be able to afford at the indicators that are in the report card, as what we say each time when we announce on affordability.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: And these prices are significantly lower than what the resale market can bear.

sections.label: HDB sale proceeds below costs
sections.summary: The proceeds HDB collects from the sale of flats is less than land and construction costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The proceeds from the sale of flats – and all this is not new; I have said this a number of times – the proceeds that HDB collects is less than land and construction costs.

sections.label: HDB Home Ownership Programme deficit
sections.summary: The passage states HDB's Home Ownership Programme ran a $3.85 billion deficit last financial year, with smaller deficits in earlier years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: That is why I explained in the opening speech, if you were listening carefully, that the development cost, which is how much we spend and how much we collect are on two parallel tracks and they converge when you see that there is a gap, a deficit, between how much you spend and how much you collect.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
