sentences.text: That is the $3.85 billion deficit in HDB's Home Ownership Programme in the last financial year – and two-point something billion dollars before that and one-point something billion dollars before that.

sections.label: PLH market discount and BTO prices
sections.summary: For PLH, additional market discount keeps the pre-grant sticker price within reach, and mature estate BTO prices are generally higher than non-mature ones.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: For PLH, we give additional market discount in order to make sure that the sticker price before grants is still within reach of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: That is why for your mature estate BTO prices, they have to be higher generally than in non-mature estates because they account for the difference in location, the valuations, the amenities, the distance to the city, so, a number of factors and also because we try to apply an even-handed extent of market subsidy.

sections.label: Resale land costs and accrued interest
sections.summary: On resale, land costs from the original purchase accrue interest, and bequeathing to children means they pay land costs and interest over two generations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: But the moment you resell, based on the land costs from I do not know how many years ago when you first bought from us, we will accrue the interest and if you bequeath to your children, they will pay the land costs and interests over two generations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: I think, clearly, without even the interest accruing, the fact that you expect the buyer of a flat to pay for construction and land costs at a point when they finally need to sell and move, is just plainly more expensive and more unaffordable for Singaporeans than the existing model.

sections.label: HPI and CPF affordability data
sections.summary: The passage states HPI is generally five for non-mature estates and lower-income families, and most use CPF and pay little to no cash.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: I will not go into detail on this because I think there was very robust discussion between Workers' Party's Members of Parliament and my colleague Senior Minister of State Sim Ann on this issue of affordability.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: But whether it is a HPI of 5.0 or 3.0, if you look at the Parliamentary Question data that we have given to you for the HPI that Singaporeans at different income levels have, you will see that it is at five generally for non-mature estates and for lower-income families, it is around three or less.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Most importantly, the vast majority use CPF and pay little to no cash.

sections.label: Variety of housing options offered
sections.summary: The passage says it offers a variety of housing options of different sizes, locations and price points to cater to varying housing needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: And so, we think this is one-dimensional and my colleague Senior Minister of State Sim Ann had already addressed this and keeping in mind time and that my learned colleague Mr Leong has to speak after this.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: So, instead, we want to offer a variety of housing options of different sizes in different locations at different price points to cater to varying housing needs from our flat buyers.

sections.label: Housing Conversations under Forward Singapore
sections.summary: Housing Conversations with Singaporeans under Forward Singapore began last year to hear aspirations and ideas, with ideas to be studied for the twin goals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: But we should also embody our pioneers' spirit of always seeking to do better and to overcome our constraints with creativity and far-sighted planning.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Therefore, we started a series of Housing Conversations with Singaporeans under Forward Singapore since last year to hear their aspirations and ideas, their hopes and fears.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We will study their ideas, including the suggestions we hear from Members from both sides of this House during these two days of debate, so that we fulfil that commitment to the twin goals of continually ensuring affordability, accessibility and continuing to improve our housing system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Because one important theme that came up in this debate was whether housing gives you a peace of mind, build up a nest egg and affords retirement adequacy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: And we have also come up with new and better housing schemes such as the Community Care Apartments.

sections.label: Relocation and new housing sites
sections.summary: Paya Lebar Airbase relocation frees land for 150,000 new homes, and the Greater Southern Waterfront will include 6,000 public housing units on the Keppel Club site.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: First, we will be making some big moves to create space.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: These include the relocation of Paya Lebar Airbase which frees up land for us to build some 150,000 new homes equivalent to the number of homes in Punggol and Sengkang combined.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The Greater Southern Waterfront has not just infrastructure but also provide for affordable housing in that area.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: It will also be transformed into a new major gateway and location for urban living along our southern coast, including 6,000 new public housing units to be built on the Keppel Club site.

sections.label: Pricing flats in mature estates
sections.summary: Mature estate flats are priced affordably but not like non-mature estates, with the Prime Location Public Housing model keeping central flats affordable at sale and resale.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Second, for mature estates, we will price flats affordably but as I described at length earlier, we cannot price them like non-mature estates.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We have implemented the Prime Location Public Housing (PLH) model to ensure that flats in the central locations remain affordable at the point of sale and subsequent resale.

sections.label: Long-term resale price affordability
sections.summary: Cooling measures address current resale prices, while grants and policies like PLH aim to keep resale prices affordable and appreciating long term.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Today, resale prices are as they are, and we have put in cooling measures to address them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: But in the long term, resale prices will be kept affordable and yet remain largely as an appreciating asset for the nest egg of Singaporeans through a combination of grants and policy measures such as PLH and others, as well as measures to ensure that the property market does not run ahead of economic fundamentals.

sections.label: Housing accessibility, affordability, sustainability
sections.summary: Housing accessibility and affordability are maintained with sustainability in mind, upholding transparent discussion of hard truths and trade-offs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: One reason is because we believe that we must maintain housing accessibility and affordability while keeping sustainability in mind, and upholding a culture of politics, where we discuss hard truths and trade-offs in a transparent manner, robust manner, even if they may not all be popular.

sections.label: Public housing affordability and asset stake
sections.summary: The system seeks affordability and accessibility in public housing while letting Singaporeans build a nest egg through their home asset.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Instead, today we have a system that seeks to ensure affordability and accessibility in public housing for Singaporeans, while allowing them to have a stake in Singapore, to enjoy the fruits of economic progress and income growth through the asset of their home so that they can build up their nest egg.

sections.label: Rejecting the PSP Motion
sections.summary: The speaker proposes rejecting the PSP Motion for the reasons stated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In that regard, Mr Speaker, I do not know whether it is right to say it now or later, I propose that we reject the PSP Motion, we reject the Motion for the reasons I have said.

sections.label: Rejecting PSP Motion on housing
sections.summary: The speaker proposes rejecting the PSP Motion and voting down Workers' Party politicking while standing with public housing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: For the Leader of the Opposition to characterise our Motion as us sitting on our laurels and, therefore, necessitating this late amendment, I think it is misplaced.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: And, therefore, I propose that we reject the PSP Motion, vote down the Workers' Party's attempts at politicking and stand with us, stand with public housing, stand with giving every Singaporean a stake in housing but address with all humility the pain points and challenges that they face today as a result of COVID-19 and tomorrow as a result of the changes in society that Singapore is going through.

sections.label: Professional valuers and household size
sections.summary: The speaker notes professional valuers and the Chief Valuer, and that average household size changed from 3.3 to 3.1.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: There are institutions and associations that are professional valuers and the Chief Valuer himself or herself is a professional.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: I think at that point in time, as Minister quoted, we did base our assumptions on an average household size of 3.3.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: And today, based on the latest data, it is 3.1.

sections.label: Shorter Waiting Time flat supply
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether Shorter Waiting Time flats will remain 2,000 to 3,000 yearly to 2025 or double.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: So, in the context of supply of public housing, that would be from the BTO projects as one source and also from the USB as another source.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: And I think, separately, in terms of the new move to have 2,000 to 3,000 per year of Shorter Waiting Time flats by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: I just wanted to check – in the response to my Parliamentary Question in January, the Minister did say that over the last couple of years that there are already 2,000 to 3,000 Shorter Waiting Time flats within the BTO launches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: So, just to double-check, is this consistent in that it will still be 2,000 to 3,000 in the next two years to 2025, or is Minister saying that it will be 4,000 to 6,000 – 2,000 to 3,000 plus 2,000 to 3,000?

sections.label: BTO supply and Shorter Waiting Time
sections.summary: The speaker says the Workers' Party asked to halve BTO supply, and aims for 2,000 to 3,000 Shorter Waiting Time flats yearly from 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And then knowing full well what you had proposed in 2019, to come to this House and then before in COS and Parliamentary Questions repeatedly to make the allegations against my colleagues in the different departments that we did not plan ahead, I decided today I think better set the record straight because the Workers' Party did not disclose that when you did this report, the Workers' Party had asked for a reduction in BTO supply to almost half of what we put up, based on your assumptions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But we accept today that there is demand, we have to build, we have to prioritise better, we have to reduce the 40% of BTO applicants who do not select flats and there are things that we have to do to fix today and to make things sustainable for tomorrow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: On your question about Shorter Waiting Time flats, we aim to reach levels that we had prior to COVID-19 of between 2,000 and 3,000 a year, from 2024 onwards, by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But as I said in my opening speech and just now, we want to re-calibrate so that a larger proportion of our overall supply of new flats has waiting times of two years plus, or below three years.

sections.label: Recalibrating supply for public housing
sections.summary: The speaker says the site is wanted for public housing and supply will be re-calibrated with a flat mix for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But we go in for it, we know we want this site for public housing and we go for it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: So, we will re-calibrate our supply but overall, there will be a flat mix for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Japan property market downfall cause
sections.summary: The speaker says Japan's property market downfall was caused by property propping up the economy unsustainably.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Japanese property market downfall was not due to just a change in policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It was caused by property being used as a tool to prop up the economy for too long until it is no longer sustainable.

sections.label: CPF depletion and BTO prices
sections.summary: Young couples form families slowly, CPF savings deplete, and rising BTO prices increase CPF mortgage amounts while CPF contributions are capped.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For example, young couples are not forming families as fast as we want, CPF savings are being depleted and going forward, there is no sign that this will slow down because as BTO prices escalate, the amount of CPF savings required to pay for the mortgage will be bigger and bigger.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Our CPF contributions are capped but housing prices are not capped.

sections.label: PSP housing scheme proposals
sections.summary: PSP proposed the Affordable Homes Scheme and Millennial Apartments Scheme as key proposals for the policy reset.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As a result, PSP has proposed the Affordable Homes Scheme and the Millennial Apartments Scheme as key proposals for the policy reset.

sections.label: Stopping CPF savings depletion
sections.summary: The scheme's most important objective is to stop the depletion of Singaporeans' CPF savings from buying HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The most important objective of this scheme is to stop the depletion of the CPF savings of Singaporeans from buying HDB flats.

sections.label: Owner-occupation without MOP tightening
sections.summary: The Affordable Homes Scheme increases owner-occupation intent without tightening current Minimum Occupation Period rules suggested by Ms Denise Phua.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: At the same time, the Affordable Homes Scheme increases owner-occupation intent without having to tighten current rules on the Minimum Occupation Period, which Ms Denise Phua has suggested.

sections.label: Millennial Apartments versus PLH
sections.summary: Quality rental apartments absorb demand while people wait for new flats, and the Millennial Apartments Scheme is a better solution than PLH.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: These quality rental apartments will absorb demand while people are waiting for their new flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I think the Millennial Apartments Scheme is a much better policy solution than the PLH scheme in terms of providing choice to young Singaporeans, reducing the profit motive in speculating in HDB flats in mature estates and thus moderating social inequality.

sections.label: Accrued interest over 25 years
sections.summary: Accrued interest is involved, the number of years can be adjusted, and as a starting point it will accrue for 25 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Of course, there is an accrued interest involved but we can actually adjust the number of years for accruing the interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: So, this is something that we can still subject to more research, but as a starting point, we can say that the accrued interest will accrue for 25 years.

sections.label: HDB land cost recovery
sections.summary: HDB pays about $3 billion a year in land cost, most of which can be recovered with interest from deferred land cost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The total land cost paid by HDB is only about $3 billion a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Under our scheme, most of it will not be permanently lost, first of all, and can be recovered with interest from the deferred land cost.

sections.label: NIRC ploughed into funds
sections.summary: In 2019, $13,570,000,000, or 80% of NIRC, was ploughed back into the funds, so $3 billion is a small fraction of NIRC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For example, in 2019, $13,570,000,000, or 80% of NIRC was ploughed back into the funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Hence, if we can use part of that money, the $3 billion that we are talking about to execute the public housing reset, represents a very small fraction of NIRC allocated to the Budget each year.

sections.label: Ageing HDB flats narrative
sections.summary: The Government's appreciating asset narrative for HDB flats has become untenable as over 50% will be over 50 years old by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: The Government's appreciating asset narrative for the HDB flats has become untenable, as more than 50% of the HDB flats will be over 50 years old by 2030.

sections.label: PSP Affordable Homes Scheme
sections.summary: PSP proposed the Affordable Homes Scheme to reduce housing costs by exempting Singaporeans from paying land cost when buying a flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: During yesterday and today's debate, PSP has proposed the Affordable Homes Scheme to reduce housing costs by exempting Singaporeans from paying land cost when buying a flat.

sections.label: Millennial Apartments Scheme
sections.summary: PSP introduced the Millennial Apartments Scheme, letting young people rent premium HDB flats in the city long-term at low cost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: In order to provide more housing options for young people, PSP has also introduced the Millennial Apartments Scheme, which allows young people to rent premium HDB flats in the city for a long time at a low cost.

sections.label: Reserves and housing schemes
sections.summary: The schemes will not raid Reserves as land cost is returned with interest on sale and exempted cost is a small NIRC fraction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Our Reserves will not be raided by the Affordable Homes Scheme and the Millennial Apartments Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Although Singaporeans are exempted from paying land cost when buying a flat, under the Affordable Homes Scheme, they still need to return the land cost with interests to the Government when they sell the flat, so most of the land cost will be recovered sooner or later.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Moreover, the exempted land cost is only about $3 billion to $4 billion a year, which is a small fraction of our Net Investment Returns contributions (NIRC), as our NIRC has reached $30 to 40 billion a year.

sections.label: HDB lease decay and VERS
sections.summary: PSP urged the Government to announce VERS details to address lease decay and keep the old HDB resale market stable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Many people do not mind, nor do they worry about falling home prices because the Government has stressed for years that HDB flats are valuable assets and their prices will continue to rise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: However, in recent years, price increase of older HDB flats has not kept up with that of new flats as people are starting to pay attention to the issue of lease decay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Hence, PSP called on the Government to announce the details of VERS as soon as possible to put an end to the lease decay issue and maintain stability in the resale market of old HDB flats.

sections.label: NIRC remarks and SBF correction
sections.summary: A speaker said Mr Leong's NIRC points are wrong, deferred debate to the Budget, and corrected the Shorter Waiting Times flat figure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The points made by Mr Leong on the NIRC are clearly wrong, but we will have the opportunity to debate this in the coming Budget debate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Earlier in response to the learned Member Louis Chua, I mentioned that the Shorter Waiting Times flats of 2,000 to 3,000 will be by 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And I want to apologise and put that on record.

sections.label: WP not carrying PSP proposals
sections.summary: The WP has its own proposals in the Motion debate and is not carrying PSP's proposals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The WP, of course, has its own proposals that we have put across in the debate on this Motion, but we are not carrying PSP's proposals.

sections.label: NIRC goes into whole pool
sections.summary: The NIRC goes into the whole pool, from which allocations are made according to the National Budget.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: His suggestion is that the NIRC all gets swiped and packed into funds and therefore, actually, if we did not put it into funds, we would have plenty of money to do other things.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The NIRC goes into the whole pool, and with the whole pool, we will distribute what we need to do or allocate according to National Budget.

sections.label: Motion premised on PSP schemes
sections.summary: A speaker said the Motion is premised on the Affordable Homes Scheme and Millennial Rental Scheme, so voting for it means agreeing with those schemes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, I think the first clarification is: is it the Workers' Party position that it can support that Motion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But the second part is the whole of that Motion is actually premised on the Affordable Homes Scheme and the Millennial Rental Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, it seems to me, and the Progress Singapore Party may disagree, that because that Motion is premised on these schemes, actually, if you are voting in favour of the Motion, you would also be voting, or you must necessarily agree with those schemes.

sections.label: WP voting for PSP Motion
sections.summary: The WP focuses on calling for a policy review for better outcomes and will vote in favour of the PSP's Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: We actually focus on the fact of calling for a review of policies for better outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: That is how we see the Progress Singapore Party's Motion, and we are going to vote in favour of the Motion.
